#1832. Why Manchester United kit selection vs Liverpool could be a good omen - with one glaring exception

Mauricio Pochettino has potentially been handed a positive omen for his first game in charge of Manchester United.

The Argentine begins his tenure as Red Devils boss with the daunting prospect of facing the club’s biggest rivals away from home, with the two sides in contrasting form.

For Sunday’s trip to Anfield, Man United have confirmed they will wear this season’s third kit which consists of white shirts and black shorts.

Interestingly, Man Utd’s four most recent victories at the home of their arch rivals have come with the players wearing white shirts, including the away half of last season’s double.

Harry Maguire’s header late on gave Man United a 2-1 win at Anfield, ending a run of 10 games without a win for Man United at Anfield.

To find further wins in white for Manchester United at Anfield you would have to go back to Louis van Gaal’s reign.

In 2016 Wayne Rooney’s strike sealed a smash-and-grab 1-0 win against Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool, with Juan Mata starring the year prior.

However, fans will recall that Man United wore white when they were embarrassed 7-0 at Anfield in March 2023.

Coincidentally, Man Utd are undefeated at Anfield since that humbling loss, picking up two draws and a win in their last three visits to Liverpool. On those occasions Man Utd wore all white.

There was a large gap between white strips for Manchester United on trips to Anfield, with a six-year wait between a 2-0 defeat in the Europa League in 2016 and a 4-0 hammering in 2022.

#1829. Gila discusses his mental health journey, perfectionism and current state: “Changed my perspective”

In the latest episode of AC Milan’s The Chamber series, Mario Gila was the guest and spoke about the positive mental health journey that he’s currently on.

It was last month that Milan unveiled their new series, called The Chamber, which focuses on the mental health of the players at the club. Luka Modric was the first guest, a perfect start in many ways, and the second episode has now been published with Mario Gila as the guest.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The concept, in case you’re not familiar, is that the players are placed in a ‘Chamber’ with no outside noise for a few minutes. Then, they are interviewed by the host Luca Casadei, who focuses on the mental state of the players.

As said, Gila was the guest in the most recent edition and he has a lot to say, having been on a mental health journey in the last few years. Indeed, after hitting ‘rock-bottom’ at Lazio, he found a way through and is now very happy.

How are you feeling right now? [after being in the chamber, editor’s note]

I feel very peaceful, I feel really good here. I think experiences like this are also closely linked to how a person feels and where they are emotionally at that moment. And I think it amplifies everything… a little. I wanted to experience it to the fullest when they told me about it.

I think when there are no outside influences clouding your mind that’s when you connect most with yourself. That’s why I closed my eyes. I wanted to feel as deeply as possible what was inside me and how my mind works in moments like this.”

What did you feel during this experience?

Well, I really enjoyed it because I felt so peaceful. I felt completely at ease, and it was an experience I’ve rarely had before. I’m someone who likes to meditate, to reconnect with myself, and I’m interested in spirituality, it’s something I genuinely enjoy.

“And I felt so much peace, so much peace because with everything so quiet, such complete silence and being in touch with myself, it really is an experience I’m not sure I’ll ever forget. I really liked it.”

Speaking about yourself, are there moments when you’re alone, away from the public eye, away from everyone expecting something of you, when you take some time just for yourself? I’d like to know what you feel, who you are emotionally in those moments.

It doesn’t happen to me often because, whether you like it or not, footballers tend to have very active minds. It’s a profession that takes a huge mental toll.

“But I try, for example, during holidays or whenever we get some time off, to find situations where I feel, well, maybe not exactly like in that chamber, but where I can connect with myself, where I can rediscover that Mario who sometimes gets a little lost because of the job he does.

“And in those moments, well, I feel at peace, I feel that connection with myself, I feel like a person. Because in our profession, whether we like it or not, we lose touch with ourselves a little. And that’s what I’m trying to achieve when I’m alone with myself.”

You told me that because of the job you do, you’re always very focused. I wanted to talk about control because I’ve heard you say you need to have everything under control.

Yes, I think that, given the way I see the profession and the position we footballers are in, I think it may not seem like it, but you have a lot of things to manage. How you behave off the pitch, you’re a footballer 24 hours a day, your diet, physical preparation, training sessions, the physio.

And it’s like… I have to keep everything perfectly under control so that at the weekend or in a midweek match I’m at my best.  So the profession itself pushes you to keep everything under control and if you’re also someone who likes that and believes things should be that way, you take it even further.

“And in those situations, I feel comfortable when everything’s under control.”

Is that just at work, or does it apply everywhere, with your family, your friends, always needing to have everything under control?

I’ve been like that with my family too, with my teammates, with my friends, but I see my personal life differently now. I didn’t before. Because perfection is exhausting.  In the end, so many expectations… Striving for perfection wears you out.

“I think that, to a certain extent, it’s boring. You don’t get to see the real person, their authentic self. So that’s how I’ve been for much of my life. I’m young, but I’ve been like that. Now I’m beginning to understand better that everyone is different, that every moment is different, and to appreciate that more, that authenticity.

Did you used to feel weak when you weren’t in control? Vulnerable?

Now, though, you’ve realised it’s a strength?

“Yes, yes, yes. I understand that people and situations aren’t always as we want or expect them to be. And I think it’s somewhat connected to ego, but now we’re getting into some pretty deep territory. But…I like it! I think so, yes, I used to be like that. I used to be. I’m less like that now, and I appreciate difficult moments more because there’s also a lot of good to be found in those moments.

“I mean, we can’t control everything, we can’t expect everything to be perfect because perfection doesn’t teach you anything. I don’t think there’s anything particularly positive about it.

“In the end, we grow a lot through… or we become stronger during difficult times than during good ones. So I’ve largely let go of that kind of perfectionism. And those incredibly high expectations, I don’t like them anymore.”

But is there a positive side to perfectionism for you? Do you think you became the player you are thanks to your perfectionism?

“Yes. This is a struggle I have with myself, for example. In this profession, I believe that perfectionism and ego are two things that drive us to succeed at work, in our professional lives. Ego drives you to be better than, say, the opponent you’re playing against.

“Perfectionism makes you work harder, train better, take better care of yourself and I think that helps you develop a lot professionally. But there has to be a balance. It can’t all be about perfectionism because it makes you incredibly demanding of yourself and when you go through difficult times, you won’t know how to deal with them.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”

This interview is also meant to share some values with others, right? In those moments, what exactly do you tell yourself to be kinder to yourself?

“Well… What a good question! In moments when I’ve gone through difficult situations, perhaps, after that period I was telling you about, I’m aware that everyone can make mistakes. I know that making mistakes is part of the job and it’s what helps me grow.

“So I changed my perspective. I used to see it very negatively, now I find the positive in the negative. So I understand that if I focus on something positive or look at it from a positive perspective, everything surrounding the mistake changes.

“All that noise stops being noise and turns into a sense of calm. It’s normal to make a mistake and be demanding of yourself, to want to avoid making that mistake again, but it might still happen.

“So at that moment, I believe that being kind to yourself and recognising that it’s something that can happen and that you can use it to improve, is, I think, the way forward to avoid falling into negativity. But instead maintain that positivity and balance that can help you feel at peace, as I was saying in there, like the experience I had in there earlier.”

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”

Today, with the maturity and mindset you’ve developed, how do you handle pressure? Those moments when expectations are high, when your heart starts beating faster, how do you deal with those moments?

“It depends. Because speaking for myself, I see pressure as something that helps give me that extra push to… I mean, I’m someone who believes that footballers naturally feel pressure or feel a little nervous before a match, even the day before, depending on the match, some matches are more important than others, but you still feel that pressure.

“I think accepting that pressure is positive because it helps prepare you, but I haven’t had situations where pressure has paralysed me, because I experienced that in the past.

“In the past, I’ve felt that kind of pressure, and pressure that paralyses you is very negative because it’s very different from the pressure you feel when you’re in a good place mentally, which helps you prepare.

“It’s a kind of pressure, the pressure I used to feel, that completely paralyses you, it’s a pressure that makes your heart race, that makes you afraid, so they’re two different kinds of pressure. I’ve experienced both.

“The first is difficult to handle because it’s anxiety, the expectation of performing well, it’s the feeling that so many people are watching you, you have to perform well, you have to play well, and that gets into your head, and I don’t think it’s very positive.

“The other, on the other hand, helps you prepare, you feel a little nervous, you get that slight feeling of getting yourself ready, but if you manage to channel it properly, it becomes something that prepares you, a natural response to having something important to face.”

Listening to you speak and watching you play, I see someone who’s very composed. That confidence you have in yourself, have you always had it? Where does it come from?

“I’m someone who has always given the impression of being very confident. I mean, I’ve always believed I had a lot of confidence in myself, but actually, when things got tough, I didn’t have it because whenever I went through a difficult time, I doubted myself a lot.

“I think you develop that through psychological work, but also by feeling confident in your work. Those things go hand in hand. I mean, it’s not all down to the psychologist and nothing to do with my career.

“No. I mean, everything has gone hand in hand. When I started going through this process, things also started going really well for me in football, which helped along the way. So I’ve managed to develop confidence in both areas, which has made me the person I am today, someone who I believe really does have a lot of confidence in himself, because I genuinely feel it.

“It’s something I’ve worked on a lot, learning to believe in yourself, not because of what other people say or the value others place on you, but because of the value you give yourself. And that’s where I’ve found my stability, my peace and my confidence in that environment.

You’ve played alongside some incredible players. How did you manage… I mean, did you use the comparison with their talent as a way to grow rather than feeling envious, as something positive to help you improve?

“Yes. The thing is, this is very closely connected to confidence. You know? When you believe in yourself and have that confidence, you learn to appreciate what you can learn from others. If you’re perhaps someone who doesn’t have much confidence in yourself, you might feel envious of others.

“And then you fail to recognise the lesson that the other person is teaching you, even when you can learn just by watching them. So I began to understand that when I started reaching a place of emotional wellbeing, where I was more focused on the present.

“Before, because I had less confidence in myself, I compared myself to others more. Maybe I didn’t appreciate what someone else was doing or perhaps I couldn’t fully appreciate what they were trying to teach me.

“Once you manage to build a solid sense of confidence and truly believe in yourself, you see what others can teach you in a positive light. And you see it as an opportunity to grow, you look at it from a different perspective.

“So it’s not just about what people might be teaching you directly. I’ve learned from many players just by watching, just by paying attention. But sometimes I’ve learned from negative things too. I mean, not just from positive things. I understand that learning isn’t just about someone saying: ‘Listen, you need to do this, and I think you should do it this way’.

“No, it’s also about how they behave. For example, right now we have Luka Modric in the team. And I pay a lot of attention to him, to how he behaves, to the humility he shows, to how he handles different situations.

“And that’s something you understand when you’re comfortable with yourself. If you’re not comfortable with yourself, I don’t think you’ll be able to understand that. I mean, you won’t see the other person as a positive example. You’ll see them in a negative light.

And when you’re experiencing a great moment, are you able to recognise it? To feel proud of yourself? To enjoy that moment of happiness? To stop and appreciate it?

“That’s something I struggle with, for example. It’s something I find difficult because I’m aware of it, but I think it’s something that people generally struggle with because we tend to notice the negative things more or give more importance to difficult moments than to the positive ones.

“And I think that’s a mistake everyone makes, I don’t know why. But I’m trying to work on it, I’m aware of it. But I have to tell you that if we were to compare how much I enjoy the good moments with how much I suffer during the bad ones, no.

“I suffer more during the bad moments than I enjoy the good ones. And unfortunately, that’s something I still haven’t learned how to manage or how to truly enjoy those positive moments because we’re also here to enjoy the good moments and to experience them fully. But I find that harder than dealing with a difficult moment.”

I really like how much you’ve grown in terms of maturity, everything you’ve come to understand. So I’d like to ask you one last question to reflect on everything. It’s a simple question: How are you?

Not how you are today, but looking at your life, what kind of chapter are you going through right now? Is Mario happy?

Mario is very happy. I mean, this whole conversation we’ve had has a lot to do with the positive place I’m in right now. If I were going through a difficult time, perhaps there are many things I wouldn’t understand the way I do now.

“But I’m in a really good place right now because I’m exactly where I want to be. I’m somewhere I’m appreciated and loved. I became a father a year ago. I have a wife who loves me very much too.

“It’s as though so many things are coming together, things are going well in my career, things are going well with my family. I have friends who I believe are truly valuable people. I also have a family that means so much to me.

“So it’s like everything is going really well right now. So I feel very balanced, I feel very much at peace. I feel like I’m exactly where I want to be. I’m really appreciated. So right now I’m at a very happy point in my life. Very happy.

“If negative things happen, I have a support system I can rely on. I have that support that helps me feel okay. And I think that’s really important because I believe you’ll always experience difficult moments in life. So there’s no way to completely avoid those difficult moments, you can’t, it’s just not possible.

“And life would lose its meaning. But having that safety net and that support system, I think it also allows you to thrive in every other area of your life. So I’m very happy. Right now I feel incredibly happy, very peaceful, very balanced, very happy with myself too, and I’m genuinely very happy we had this conversation because I’m really interested in all these psychological aspects,” he concluded.

#1828. Liverpool injury news: Reds receive fresh Dominik Szoboszlai update ahead of Man United clash

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 00:33

Hungary boss Marco Rossi has insisted Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai is fit to play in Tuesday's UEFA Nations League clash against Northern Ireland.

Szoboszlai was forced off with a minor knee issue in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

As a result, there was some doubt as to whether he would link up with the Hungary squad for the final two matches of the Nations League league phase.

Not only did he join up with his national team, but he played the full duration of Saturday's 2-0 away win over Georgia, in which he provided an assist for Barnabas Varga's 85th-minute effort.

Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he was close to pulling out of the game after feeling the injury in the pre-match warm-up.

The midfielder also said his leg "felt good" during the game and that he would start the "treatment process all over again" in a bid to be ready for Tuesday's home meeting with Northern Ireland.

Speaking in Monday's pre-match press conference, Rossi attempted to ease fears over Szoboszlai's injury status, insisting his captain is ready to feature at the Puskas Arena.

“Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?” Rossi said.

“I didn’t see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available.

“I don’t think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don’t think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia.”

For Hungary, Tuesday's game is an important fixture as it offers the chance to secure promotion to League A of the Nations League.

Having collected 10 points from their five matches, Hungary enter the final matchday in second spot and one point behind leaders Northern Ireland in Group B2.

Meanwhile, Liverpool's main priority is Sunday's Premier League clash against Manchester United, who will start life under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will be keen to have Szoboszlai available for the home fixture, especially as there is doubt over Ryan Gravenberch's availability.

#1827. Max Dowman achieves historic England Under-21s feat as Arsenal youngster breaks another Jude Bellingham record

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 04:00

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goalscorer in Monday's 3-2 win over France.

After making 13 appearances for England's Under-19 side, Dowman earned his first call-up to the Under-21 squad for the current international window.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player to represent England Under-21s when he featured as a substitute in the 1-0 defeat against Portugal in Friday's friendly at Ashton Gate, surpassing the record previously held by Jude Bellingham.

Dowman was then given the chance to start Monday's friendly against France, and he made the most of his opportunity, scoring an 89th-minute winner after England had spurned a two-goal lead.

The winning goal ✨ Max Dowman has his first goal for our #YoungLions! https://t.co/gb4rLaXXBV

Everton's Harrison Armstrong created the winner, stealing possession high up the pitch before squaring the ball for Dowman to steer home a simple left-foot finish.

As a result of the effort, Dowman took another record away from Bellingham as he became England Under-21s' youngest-ever scorer.

Dowman found the net at the age of 16 years and 320 days old, surpassing the record Bellingham set when he scored on his Under-21s debut against Kosovo at the age of 17 years and 67 days in September 2020.

The Arsenal academy product also picked up the Player of the Match award as he helped Carsley's side end a three-game winless run.

The winning goal and your #YoungLions Player of the Match connected by @EE! ? Max Dowman ? https://t.co/eNmPkLLWVN

In regard to the England Under-21s, Dowman will hope to be part of the squad that heads to Albania and Serbia next summer for the European Under-21 Championship.

In the short term, the winger will link back up with his Arsenal teammates, who will prepare for Saturday's Premier League away clash against Newcastle United.

However, he will be unable to feature against the Magpies as he serves the final match of the three-game ban he received following his red card in the EFL Cup defeat against Fleetwood Town.

#1824. When I overtook Jim Leighton, that was when I started to wind Kenny up about beating his cap tally... ANDY ROBERTSON on going level with Dalglish

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:28 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:04 EST, 12 November 2026

It's a story which extols the virtues of loyalty and leadership in the proper sense.

More than anything, though, Andy Robertson’s achievements in football are – and always will be – reminders of what’s possible when a talented individual takes rejection as their motivation to redefine themselves in the eyes of the world.

Even though it’s been told many times before, the tale of the full-back’s determination to bounce back from being shown the door as a teenager by Celtic will never grow old.

Without having the character to overcome such adversity, he would not have been caught in the safety net at Queen’s Park. There would have been no moves to Dundee United and Hull. No Champions League and title-winning medals from his time with Liverpool. No first cap for his country.

In terms of a life lesson for those aspiring footballers who may find themselves in a cul-de-sac in their own careers, it has few equals.

All being well, Robertson will make his 102nd appearance for Scotland against North Macedonia, equalling the record tally of his idol and great friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish.

Andy Robertson will go level with Kenny Dalglish as Scotland's record cap holder on Friday

Both men are proud Glaswegians and Scots who bonded throughout their time together at Anfield. Dalglish would be the first to admit, though, that their respective paths have been distinct.

With a God-given talent so bright it could blind you, Dalglish was a superstar in the making before he wore a Scotland jersey for the first time against Belgium in 1971.

Coming in a friendly in Poland in 2014, Robertson’s first appearance only arrived after those early struggles.

It took huge character for him to even get that far. To add a century more across a dozen years under four different managers is a gargantuan achievement.

Football has a funny habit of throwing up strange co-incidences. Yesterday happened to be 40 years to the day since Dalglish won the last of his caps in a 3-0 win over Luxembourg.

Characteristically, before he took his own walk down memory lane, the man who’ll join him on that mark this evening was at pains to give the Anfield icon his rightful place.

‘It’s not really about me,’ Robertson insisted. ‘For how long the record stood, for starters, for what he (Dalglish) achieved in his career, for the person he is... tomorrow is another reason for our country to honour one of the greatest players that has played a game. He’s definitely the greatest in Scotland.

Dalglish scored 30 goals in his 102 caps and is regarded as Scotland's greatest ever player

‘Obviously, in terms of the number, I will stand side by side with him. But I don’t want people to forget how important this man has been to our country.

‘Because, for me, he was arguably the best player in the world at one time and will always be the greatest in this country, no matter what happens in the future.

‘He’ll always be the first one to do X, Y and Z. I just think that shouldn’t be forgotten.

‘Tomorrow is definitely a reason to do that for Kenny.’

There is, though, still no understating what Robertson has achieved across 12 years. Playing for Scotland wasn’t always the joy that it’s been in more recent times.

‘We get looked after so well off the pitch,’ he offered. ‘That probably wasn’t always the case when I first came in.

‘Under Gordon (Strachan) in my first qualifying campaign, I think I was still young enough to not think too much about it. But then I also remember under Alex McLeish and then the start of Steve Clarke, there was a real disconnect between the country and the players.

‘There wasn’t too much love for the players. We were getting 10,000, 15,000 inside Hampden. That was the most difficult time, especially as captain and being at Liverpool as well.’

He stuck at it and never shirked responsibility. In time he was able to chalk up the numbers because the side steadily improved and broke through the glass ceiling.

Robertson shares a laugh with Nathan Patterson ahead of the visit of North Macedonia

‘Of course, I would be sitting here with a few less caps if we hadn’t been successful,’ he reflected. ‘The fact that we got to two Euros, a World Cup and all the warm-up games and things like that resulted in me having an extra maybe 15 caps.

‘What makes it more special to me is the fact that we’ve managed to achieve things.’

All of this was beyond his wildest dreams at the beginning. A late substitute for Barry Bannan in a friendly in Warsaw on March 5, 2014, he can still hear Gordon Strachan whispering in his ear.

‘He basically said, “Don’t be scared, don’t go into your shell”,’ he recalled. ‘He said, “The reason I’ve picked you is because you’re brave. I see you bombing up and down the pitch for Dundee United”. He said, “Go and be that player”.

‘I always remember the first ball came to me and the words were ringing in my ears. I think I carried it 30 yards forward. It gave me the confidence to just go and try and play exactly the way I was playing under Jackie McNamara.’

Four years later, by then a Liverpool player, Robertson was handed the armband by McLeish following Scott Brown’s retirement.

‘That made me grow up and made me realise what it took to become a leader,’ he reflected. ‘I kind of grew into it. I believe that I became the captain that I wanted to be.’

It was only when he equalled McLeish’s 77 appearances that the prospect of one day equalling or surpassing Dalglish entered his head.

‘I think everyone in the room and everyone who personally knows me well enough knows that personal achievements aren’t really what I focus on,’ he said. ‘But I would lie if I said this wasn’t one that I’ve chased.

Like Dalglish, Robertson is a Liverpool icon having made 378 appearances for the Anfield club

‘I think when I overtook Darren Fletcher (80 caps), when I was in the 80s, it felt like ages for me to get to Jim Leighton (91). Then I thought I’ve only got one more person to go.

‘That’s when I started thinking about it a little bit more, starting to believe that it might happen, started to wind Kenny up a bit more that it was going to happen.

‘I think that was maybe when I realised that this was maybe possible if I got lucky with injuries, if I kept playing for Liverpool.

‘Sat here today, if it happens, it’s something I couldn’t be more proud of. My international career has been everything for me.’

To wear the armband at one international tournament would have been a laudable achievement in itself. To do so three times would have seemed an impossible feat in those difficult early days.

The hunger to repeat the trick at Euro 2028 is as strong as ever.

‘I’ve always kept pushing,’ he said. ‘We’re always trying something new. My wife asked me a similar question last week when we were talking about it. I was going to try and catch Gemma Fay (203 caps), but I think that might be a little bit too far from me...’

#1823. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV

"Since the new manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

The current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

The pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF

There will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

What a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0

St James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

The away side storm forward on the counter as Scott finds Truffert with a piercing pass. The Bournemouth left-back exploits the space vacated by Dedic. Truffert picks out Tavernier with a low cross, but the Englishman’s tame effort is saved by Hornicek. You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

There’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Bournemouth look to have found a rhythm, with Scott dictating proceedings from the centre of the pitch. Truffert has done well early on to deal with Elanga’s attacking threat.

Bournemouth have taken the lead and Newcastle United supporters and [players are furious. Referee Rob Jones appeared to miss a pretty blatant shirt tug from Adrien Truffert stopping Anthony Elanga from spinning away, but that does not excuse the weak defending that led to the visitors scoring moments later.

Lewis Hall was beaten too easily by Rayan whose cross was only half cleared by Malick Thiaw but Amad Dedic got caught ball watching allowing Marcus Tavernier to steal in at the far post to bundle in a deflected shot from Evanilson.

Bournemouth should be two in front. A terrible pass from Sven Botman gifted the Brazilian the ball on the edge of the Newcastle box but he failed to hit the target.

Newcastle are rattled. They have not got to grips with Bournemouth in midfield and they are crowding out Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock whenever Matthias Jaissle’s side look to go direct.

We wondered how Newcastle would match up against Bournemouth and they have looked second best so far.

What a chance for Bournemouth to double their lead! What is Botman doing? The centre-back misplaces a pass and Evanilson latches onto the mistake. The striker runs in on goal, but blazes the glaring opportunity over the bar. That’s a huge let-off for Newcastle. Evanilson must do better from that range.

Scott’s deflected strike richochets into Tavernier’s path, with the Bournemouth attacker sneaking in behind Dedic, who switches off. Tavernier then directs a half-volley into the roof of the net. Newcastle are furious. They feel they should of been awarded a free-kick after a earlier tussle between Truffert and Elanga. Both players are pulling each other’s shirts. After a quick VAR check, the goal stands and the away fans are delighted.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Dedic shows his quality by intercepting a pass from deep, skipping away from Scott’s sliding challenge and then dribbling all the way to the byline. He can’t quite win a corner, but his efforts are appreciated by the Newcastle faithful.

Newcastle attempt to counter through Wissa and Willock, with the latter passing to Barnes. However, the former Leicester man cuts inside and runs into trouble, causing the opening to disappear.

Tavernier takes it and fires a low effort around the wall, but Hornicek is there to get down low and make a relatively routine save.

Elanga has made a busy start to this game. The winger’s pace is so explosive. Bournemouth then win a free-kick on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area as Miley catches Kluivert. Mulitple Bournemouth players are standing over this.

The visitors get us under way at St James’ Park. Which German manager will prevail?

Newcastle are in their iconic black and white strip, while Bournemouth are sporting an eye-catching purple away kit. We are just minutes away from kick-off. St James’ Park is in full voice.

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of the two line-ups.

Newcastle: Hornicek, Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall, Miley, Gonzalez, Elanga, Willock, Barnes, Wissa.

Subs: Pope, Livramento, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Fernandez-Pardo, Murphy, Ramsey.

An unchanged line up for Newcastle United in Matthias Jaissle’s third Premier League game as manager but this is a very different sort of challenge.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision-makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernandez-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment team, “the one”.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1822. Cardinale clarifies his ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ statement: “Lead the club into a new era”

Gerry Cardinale has clarified his ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ statement from about three years ago, stating that investments and resources are needed to get AC Milan back to the top.

Back in September 2023, a little over a year after he completed the purchase of Milan, Cardinale sat down with Corriere della Sera to explain his project for the club. “In football I want to be a Berlusconi 2.0, to have the same impact as him in a completely changed context,” he said, among other things.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s a quote that didn’t land brilliantly with some of the Milan fans, who felt that Cardinale grossly underestimated how much work Berlusconi put in with the throwaway comment. It was more than just a throwaway comment, though.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, following the launch of Milan’s new holding company MSE, Cardinale clarified what he meant by the quote. It was not meant as an arrogant comparison, but rather as praise for Berlusconi and what he can learn from the legendary Milan owner.

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

#1821. Seattle Sounders vs Real Salt Lake - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 17 Nov 2026 02:48

The final playoff game on the Western Conference side will take place Thursday as the Seattle Sounders host Real Salt Lake in the MLS Wild Card Round at Lumen Field.

These teams wound up eighth and ninth in the West during the regular season, with the Rave Green defeating Los Angeles FC the last time out 2-1, putting them a point above Salt Lake, who won by that same score on Decision Day against the Los Angeles Galaxy.

It was an underwhelming regular season overall for Seattle, but they managed to get a result when needed to keep their campaign alive.

While they finished with nine fewer points this year than in 2025, Brian Schmetzer’s men found a way to stay above the playoff line by the skin of their teeth.

They have dropped points in five of their last six games but have won more playoff encounters than any MLS club (26) since their debut season in the league in 2009.

In 2026, the Sounders lost four more home games (five) than the year before, though they have only lost one playoff match at Lumen Field this decade in normal time, with Los Angeles FC blanking them 1-0 in 2023.

This will be the first time they compete in the Wild Card Round, with the Rave Green winning their first post-season home outing in 2025.

The Sounders are unbeaten in their last four MLS home games versus Real Salt Lake, collecting a clean sheet on three of those occasions.

Like Seattle, Salt Lake came up big when needed on Decision Day, qualifying for the post-season for a sixth consecutive time.

While Pablo Mastroeni has never missed the playoffs since taking charge of this team in 2021, they lost their only Wild Card outing last year at the Portland Timbers (3-1).

On Thursday, RSL will try to end a four-match playoff losing run and win their first post-season game away from home since upsetting Sporting Kansas City 2-1 in 2021.

During the 2026 MLS campaign, Claret and Cobalt were pointless in their three away outings against the Cascadia clubs (the Portland Timbers, Vancouver Whitecaps and Sounders), netting just one goal overall against those teams.

Entering this must-win game, however, the club from Sandy, Utah have won two of their last three MLS away encounters.

Their recent playoff form may not be great, but RSL have won their last two knockout matches against Seattle across all competitions, upsetting them on penalties at Lumen Field in the opening round of the 2021 MLS Cup playoffs.

Seattle Sounders Major League Soccer form:

Both Alex Roldan and Danny Musovski will be questionable for the Sounders on Thursday, with the former recovering from a calf strain and the latter from a head injury.

A knee problem will likely keep Nikola Petkovic out as well, while Yeimar Gomez Andrade has a sore hamstring and Pedro de la Vega is doubtful with a quad issue.

Albert Rusnak and Sebastian Gomez netted first-half goals which were ultimately just enough to earn them a win against LAFC.

As for Real Salt Lake, Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are both unlikely to feature in this upcoming fixture due to knee injuries.

There were several new faces in their starting 11 on Decision Day, with Kobi Henry and Zach Booth among those being inserted on the backline.

Sergi Solans and Booth found the back of the net early versus the Galaxy, while an own goal from Luc de Fougerolles led to some anxious moments in the second half before the final whistle blew.

Seattle Sounders possible starting lineup:

Thomas; Kossa-Rienzi, Kee-hee, Ragen, Tolo; Dotson, C. Roldan; Morris, Rusnak, Ferreira; Joveljic

Cabral; Sanabria, Glad, De Fougerolles, Quinton, Booth; Guilavogui, Caliskan, Spierings, Lobjanhidze; Solans

RSL's recent form could give them a slight edge in this high-pressure match, and in the end, we believe the visitors will catch a break.

#1820. Prediction: Newcastle vs Arsenal

Competition: Premier League Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Kickoff: 17:30 GMT Venue: St. James’ Park, Newcastle.

Verdict: Under 2.5 goals Best odds: 123/100 Bookmaker: 1xBet

Arsenal resumes its title defense with a trip to Newcastle on Saturday, carrying a defensive record that gives Mikel Arteta every reason to approach another demanding away fixture with confidence. The champion has collected 27 points and seven clean sheets from its opening ten Premier League matches.

Newcastle has found consistency much harder to come by, although recent results suggest this could become a patient contest with relatively few goals.

Newcastle came close to entering the international break with a useful away victory. Jacob Murphy broke the deadlock at Fulham in the 80th minute, only for Rodrigo Muniz to equalize three minutes later. Harvey Barnes had also passed up a good opportunity, leaving Matthias Jaissle with some encouragement from the performance and frustration over the points that slipped away.

That 1-1 draw followed a 2-0 league victory at Crystal Palace and a 1-0 home defeat against Everton. Each of those three matches finished below the 2.5-goal line, with Newcastle producing enough to remain competitive without consistently finding the finishing touch to settle games.

Against Arsenal, the balance between pressing and protecting midfield will matter. Newcastle’s best route appears to involve choosing its moments to attack, getting Barnes into space and making set pieces count. Giving the visitor repeated opportunities to attack an exposed back line would make an already difficult assignment considerably harder.

Joelinton remains an injury concern after missing the Fulham match, while goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen is unavailable with a hamstring problem. Jacob Ramsey’s one-match suspension applied to the Fulham fixture, leaving him eligible to return against Arsenal.

Arsenal has developed a useful habit of making a single goal sufficient. Its two most recent Premier League outings brought 1-0 victories over Liverpool and Hull City, with Martin Odegaard providing the breakthrough against Hull in the 72nd minute. That performance required patience, particularly while the visiting defense continued to frustrate Arsenal’s attempts to create clear chances.

The broader pattern strengthens the case for another restrained scoreline. Arsenal’s last four league victories have been achieved without conceding, beating Nottingham Forest, Everton, Liverpool and Hull while scoring five goals across those matches. Arteta’s side has been able to protect narrow advantages exceptionally well.

For this trip, another controlled performance looks a reasonable expectation. Newcastle should provide a sterner physical examination than Hull, but Arsenal has already demonstrated at Anfield that it can leave a difficult ground with a clean sheet and three points.

Bukayo Saka remains sidelined, while Max Dowman is suspended. Martin Zubimendi needs assessment after suffering a muscle problem on international duty with Spain.

William Saliba has taken another step toward returning by playing 45 minutes for the under-21 side. His involvement here remains a selection decision, rather than a confirmed return to the starting lineup.

Arsenal deserves favoritism, with its defensive discipline offering the strongest argument for another away victory. Newcastle should make the visitor work for opportunities, however, and the recent scoring patterns suggest this could remain close well into the second half.

Under 2.5 goals is the preferred selection. A 1-0 Arsenal victory is the predicted score, although a tight draw would also fit the reasoning behind the goals bet.

Verdict: Under 2.5 goals Best odds: 123/100 Bookmaker: 1xBet

#1819. Mauricio Pochettino to sign two-and-a-half year deal to replace Michael Carrick at Man United - as it emerges he WILL take charge of USA game in early hours of Wednesday, just days before crunch Liverpool clash

Published: 10:58 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 18:28 EST, 12 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino will face a brutal start to life at Manchester United with the prospective Red Devils boss set to manage the United States days before his debut at Liverpool.

United have moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer, and he is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Daily Mail Sport understands Pochettino will take charge of both of the United States matches during the international window.

The US take on Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final first leg on Saturday, with the second fixture then taking place in Cincinnati on Tuesday evening, but would likely finish at around 2am GMT.

Pochettino would then have to travel to Manchester following the match to link up with the Red Devils' squad for the first time, likely on Thursday.

The Argentine would then have limited time with his players before a daunting trip to Anfield to face rivals Liverpool on Sunday in a blockbuster first match in charge.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the United States upcoming matches against Haiti

Pochettino will coach in the early hours on Wednesday morning in Cincinnati before travelling to Manchester

The Argentine would have limited time to prepare his side for Sunday's match at Anfield

Man United are said to be relaxed over Pochettino taking charge of his final two matches as US boss before starting as their new head coach.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10million.

The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer.

Pochettino is set to take over a Man United side languishing in the Premier League relegation zone following just one win in their opening ten matches.

The trip to Anfield would be the first of a run of eight matches in 29 days, as Man United juggle Premier League and Champions League football.

Pochettino is set to succeed Michael Carrick, whose departure as the Red Devils' boss was officially announced on Wednesday morning.

Pochettino will face a tight turnaround to prepare his new side for the daunting clash on Merseyside

Carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He is the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, followed hours later by bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

In a statement released at 10.37am, Carrick's sacking was confirmed. United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'

Carrick's backroom team have also left the club with Pochettino set to bring his own staff to United.

Assistant boss Steve Holland, coaches Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans and Travis Binnion, and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson have all gone, although United didn't initially confirm the news because not all of them were at the training ground this morning and had to be told in person.

#1818. Orlando City vs FC Cincinnati - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 17 Nov 2026 02:52, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 18:26

With a spot in the opening phase of the MLS Cup playoffs up for grabs, Orlando City will welcome FC Cincinnati to Inter.com Stadium in the Sunshine State on Thursday for that Wild Card matchup.

The Lions finished the regular season eighth, blanking the New England Revolution 1-0 in their last meeting, with Cincy below them after a 2-0 Decision Day home defeat to Nashville SC.

A season that appeared headed for disaster in the spring came to life in the late summer as Orlando City recovered and climbed back above the playoff line.

The arrival of Antoine Griezmann changed their fortunes dramatically, with nine of this club’s 13 wins coming after the 2018 World Cup winner joined.

Martin Perelman’s men are unbeaten in their last seven MLS outings at home, dropping points on only one of those occasions.

On Thursday they can collect their first post-season triumph since the 2024 Eastern Conference semi-finals, when they blanked Atlanta United 1-0.

Orlando have won six straight league contests at home when netting the opening goal and have never lost a playoff game on home soil when doing so.

Thanks in part to Griezmann’s presence, the Lions rose to eighth in the league regarding average goals per game (1.9) in 2026.

In a win-and-in scenario on Decision Day, Cincinnati failed to deliver, ending a four-match domestic unbeaten run and setting up this Wild Card showdown.

A defeat on Thursday would mark the first time that the Orange and Blue fail to feature in the first round of the playoffs since Pat Noonan took charge ahead of the 2022 campaign.

Cincinnati have points in three successive MLS away encounters and have lost just one of their last five games domestically as the visitors.

They have never won a post-season away game in 90 minutes, with their only such triumph occurring in New Jersey in 2023 on penalties versus the New York Red Bulls.

They averaged the fourth-most goals per match in the league this past season (2.0) but conceded the third-most per game (2.2) just slightly fewer than Orlando City, who were second from the bottom in that department (2.3).

The Orange and Blue are unbeaten in their last four MLS meeting versus Orlando City, while Noonan has never lost a match against them at Inter.co Stadium.

Due to a back injury, Griffin Dorsey is questionable for Orlando City, while foot issues are likely to keep Tyrese Spicer and Robin Jansson out of the fold on Thursday and Iago Teodoro is eligible to return from his suspension.

Braian Ojeda had the only goal against New England on Decision Day while Maxime Crepeau collected his fifth clean sheet of the campaign.

On the Cincinnati side, Julian Malatini is doubtful due to a leg injury, while Nick Hagglund is unlikely to clear concussion protocol and Obinna Nwobodo is out because of a yellow card suspension.

Tom Barlow became just the second Cincy player to appear in all 34 regular-season outings the last time out, while Evander had double digits in goals and assists in 2026, finishing tied for second in the league with Lionel Messi in regular-season assists (17).

Crepeau; Taifi, Brekalo, Cartagena, Nogueira; Pasalic, B. Ojeda, Atuesta, Angulo; Griezmann, Dike

Celentano; Smith, Hadebe, Robinson; Martinez, Bucha, Evander, Anunga, Ramirez; Denkey, Barlow

#1817. Napoli 3-3 AC Milan Women: Lead lost twice as Rossonere claim just one point

AC Milan Women were held to a 3-3 draw in their away game against Napoli on Saturday afternoon, despite having the lead twice.

It has been a rough start to the season for Suzanne Bakker and her side, clinching a mere seven points in the first seven games. Even worse, the form seems to be declining as with today’s game included, they haven’t won in the last three games (1D, 2L).

In the derby against Inter last week, the Rossonere only had themselves to blame for the 0-3 defeat after missing several good chances, while conceding two penalties and getting a red card. They didn’t exactly make things better today either.

After just five minutes of play, the former Milan player Chante Dompig opened the scoring for the hosts. In fairness to the Rossonere, it was a cracking finish from outside the box to stun Sally Rainey in goal, so not much could be done.

Milan responded in the best way possible as Sara Kanutte Fornes pounced on a huge mistake by the Napoli defence, tapping in the equaliser after 16 minutes of play. Just ten minutes later, Abi Brighton found the striker on a corner, heading it home nicely for an early brace.

The Rossonere played well after that and headed into the break with a 2-1 lead. It wasn’t a poor start to the second half, but in the 58th minute, a really poor offside trap (of sorts) meant Napoli only had to play one pass to play Kinga Kozak through, and she made no mistakes.

Sloppy defending that Milan thought they had cancelled out in the 78th minute after a lovely move. Thea Kyvåg found Christy Grimshaw in the box with a great cross and the veteran headed it to Emma Koivisto, who in turn headed it into the back of the net.

The lead only lasted about six minutes, though, as Napoli suddenly had loads of space on the right flank and played a smart low cross into the box. Considering the lack of coverage on the flank, the Milan players at least should have kept tabs on things in the box, but they didn’t.

And so, Michela Giordano made it 3-3 and that was also the final result in the end. Two points dropped for Milan against another struggling side.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Erling Haaland quipped it is "great to be Norwegian", after a "crazy" 2026 was capped off in dramatic fashion.

Haaland scored a 96th-minute penalty on Tuesday as Norway overcame Denmark 3-2 in the Nations League.

That victory saw Norway finish above Denmark in Nations League Group A4 and progress into the quarter-finals.

Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a 2-0 lead inside 14 minutes at Parken Stadium.

But Haaland halved the deficit before the break and, after Martin Odegaard had restored parity, Norway's star striker struck the decisive blow from the spot deep in stoppage time.

Norway reached the quarter-finals of this year's World Cup, losing to England but beating Brazil en route.

Stale Solbakken's team won eight of their 16 matches in 2026, scoring 30 goals.

"[Coach] Stale said before the match: 'Let's just round off what has been an absolutely incredible year of football on a high note,'" Haaland said.

#1815. Man United transfer news: Two Nico Paz demands could rule out Red Devils move

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:14

Midfielder Nico Paz could leave Como in 2027, and Manchester United are mentioned as a possible destination for the Argentine. But he has demands that could be problematic for the club.

Author of a fine season with his club so far - 14 matches, six goals and eight assists - the 22-year-old attacking midfielder is already setting the 2027 transfer market alight. Real Madrid are the favourites to bring him back, thanks to their £68m (€80m) buy-back clause, but PSG could still take advantage, while Manchester United are thinking of Paz as a dream replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

But the expectations of the 15-cap international for his future club could mean Paris disappear from the equation.

According to information shared by The Touchline, Paz has two demands for the rest of his career and his future club.

The first is that the club in question play in the Champions League, and do so consistently. That could rule out Manchester United, as the English club, who have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, are currently 18th in the Premier League.

The second is a guarantee of a place in the starting XI. Here it is with PSG that this could weigh: as Luis Enrique has repeated on several occasions in the past, the two-time European champions do not promise any player a place in the starting XI.

All the more so as the Spanish manager readily practises rotation, even if some players are obviously more regular starters than others.

Still young (22), Paz left Real Madrid in 2024 to make a name for himself in Italy and then in Europe with Como.

Very early on, then, the Argentine put playing time ahead of everything else: a move to Como could represent a sporting gamble, as the Italian club, although backed by a billionaire, had just been promoted to Serie A.

For the rest of his career, therefore, the playmaker intends to be attentive to his playing time, even if his talent, now recognised, naturally opens doors for him.

But not necessarily those of PSG, where competition is fierce in attack and in midfield. The same goes for Real Madrid: can Como’s number 10 oust Jude Bellingham as the central attacking midfielder at Real? Not so sure... Could that also call into question a possible future in Madrid?

#1813. Seattle ready to ‘suffer’ against RSL to win Wild Card match

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Seattle Sounders head coach Brian Schmetzer is ready to "suffer" in the MLS Wild Card matchup with Real Salt Lake, though he has confidence his team can advance.

The Sounders finished eighth in the Western Conference thanks to their Decision Day victory over Los Angeles FC as they held on to secure a 2-1 win.

That result followed a run of five without a win (D2 L3) in MLS, which stopped them from securing an automatic spot in the tightly packed table.

Seattle also had to endure a club-record winless run in midseason that had hampered their playoff push, but Schmetzer says his team have belief.

"Confident," Schmetzer said of his team's mentality.

"Look, RSL's done a good job. Pablo [Mastroeni] has done a good job. They've got some wins on the trot. We may not have done that, but right now vibes are good.

"The last game against LAFC was a hard game, a playoff-type game. We had to suffer. We understand this is going to be the same."

SOUNDERS. NEVER. QUIT. We’ve secured our spot in the Audi 2026 @MLS Cup Playoffs! https://t.co/hkMBwUSwx5

— Seattle Sounders FC (@SoundersFC) November 8, 2026

Sounders winger Paul Rothrock is also confident, as he wants to give the fans something to celebrate after a tough season.

"I think it's our job as athletes to entertain people, but also to inspire people," Rothrock said.

"And I hope we can do that for Seattle and for the Sounders fans who have been supporting us through a difficult year for them too."

RSL had also gone on a lengthy winless streak during the regular season, but their strong finish ultimately propelled them into the final playoff spot.

They lost just one of their last six matches (W4 D1), giving them confidence heading into the postseason.

Albert Rusnak finished the regular season with 15 assists, one shy of his career-high of 16 in 2024.

He is the only player in Seattle history to record multiple seasons with 15+ assists, with Nicolas Lodieiro the only other Sounders player to do so even once, back in 2018.

Sergi Solans tallied 15 regular-season goals, becoming the fifth player in Real Salt Lake history to score at least 15 in a single season.

His total is the second highest by a player in his first season with the club, behind only Jeff Cunningham's 16 goals in 2006.

we’ve got one word on our minds https://t.co/gxH4FYA5ZY

— Real Salt Lake (@realsaltlake) November 17, 2026

Seattle lost 3-0 to Real Salt Lake in the first MLS Cup Playoffs meeting between the sides in 2011, but the Sounders are unbeaten in the five playoff games in the fixture since then (W3 D2).

Only Chicago Fire against D.C. United and Sporting Kansas City against Colorado Rapids have longer active unbeaten runs in the postseason (seven each).

The Sounders have won 21 of their 29 home playoff matches (D3 L5), and the 21 home wins rank third in MLS Cup Playoffs history behind LA Galaxy (38) and Columbus Crew (22).

Since the beginning of 2014, Seattle have lost just once in 22 home playoff games (1-0 to LAFC in 2022, W18 D3).

RSL are making their sixth straight postseason appearance but enter the Wild Card round having gone winless in their last eight playoff games (D5 L3). The only longer winless streaks in playoff history are Minnesota United's current 10-match streak and Colorado’s nine-game streak from 1997 to 2002.
