#1795. Prince William leads tributes to Harry Kane as England captain breaks appearance record with 126th cap: Royal presents star with shirt marking occasion as Wembley celebrates milestone

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 14:45 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026

Prince William led tributes for Harry Kane as Wembley honoured the England captain on reaching his record-breaking 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday.

Kane, who became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or last month, celebrated another remarkable feat as he surpassed legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history.

After walking out with his four children for kick-off, followed by his England team-mates, the Bayern Munich forward first held his Ballon d'Or trophy aloft to Wembley's buoyant crowd, soaking up the celebrations.

Shilton approached the England captain to present him with a medal displaying his achievement, before Kane's former Spurs team-mate Luka Modric continued the tributes by offering him another gift.

Prince William then walked on to the pitch to shake Kane's hand and present him with a framed shirt, bearing the words 'Kane 126'.

As well as holding the record for England's most capped player, the 33-year-old striker is also England's highest ever scorer with 91 goals, ahead of Wayne Rooney and Sir Bobby Charlton who netted 53 and 49 respectively during their careers.

Prince William shakes Harry Kane's hand as he celebrates the England captain's record cap

The Prince led tributes as Wembley honoured Kane ahead of England's clash with Croatia

Kane, accompanied by his four children on the pitch, held his Ballon d'Or aloft to supporters

Prince William applauded 'brilliant and remarkable' Kane on his Ballon d'Or triumph with a personal social media message after the ceremony in London.

The Prince of Wales, signing his message off with his personal 'W' initial, posted on Instagram: 'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or! What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

Kane, who has been widely regarded as a model professional and humble superstar during his career, admitted he still has an ego of sorts in an interview on the eve of his record-breaking England cap.

Asked if he has an ego, Kane replied: ‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!

'But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

On becoming England's highest appearance maker, he joked that some of his current Three Lions team-mates might catch his total by the end of their careers.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ he added. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!

He has passed Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history - with 126 to his name

Kane receives a gift from ex-Spurs team-mate and fellow Ballon d'Or winner Luka Modric

’In football, you’ve never completed it. No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has. This is no time to rest. If anything, I've got better year on year, and the numbers have got better.

'While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible, and I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I want to make sure that I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that, whenever that day comes, I can say, “I’ve done everything possible. I have this record, I don’t have this record, but it doesn’t matter, I can sleep well at night”.’

#1794. Real Madrid transfer news: Los Blancos eyeing moves for 'impressive' Brighton & Hove Albion duo

By Matt Law | 17 Nov 2026 08:45, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 08:47

Real Madrid are reportedly interested in signing Brighton & Hove Albion duo Luka Vuskovic and Chema Andres.

Brighton have been outstanding this season, especially in England's top flight, with the Seagulls currently sitting second in the Premier League table behind the champions Arsenal.

A record of seven wins, one draw and two defeats has seen the Seagulls pick up 22 points, while they are the leading goalscorers in the Premier League this term with 26.

Seven goals conceded represents the second-best defensive record, meanwhile, and Vuskovic has been a standout performer following his arrival from Tottenham Hotspur.

The 19-year-old has scored once and provided two assists in 16 appearances for Brighton this term, and his performances have already led to a host of attention.

Real Madrid are in the market for another centre-back, and according to TEAMtalk, the Spanish giants are huge admirers of Vuskovic.

The Croatia international has a contract at the Amex until the summer of 2031, with the option of a further year, placing Brighton in a strong position.

However, the Seagulls will find it difficult to keep hold of him on a long-term basis if the likes of Real Madrid begin a serious pursuit of the teenager.

Real Madrid are also allegedly keeping a close eye on the performances of their former player Andres, who moved to Brighton from Stuttgart over the summer.

The 21-year-old has one goal and one assist in nine appearances for Brighton this term.

Andres, who is a 6ft 4in defensive midfielder, played for Real Madrid between 2018 and 2025, progressing through the youth system to the first team.

The Spaniard played three times for Real Madrid's senior team during the 2024-25 campaign before moving to Stuttgart, featuring on 41 occasions for the German club ahead of a move to the Premier League.

There have previously been claims that Los Blancos have some form of buyback option on Andres, but Brighton are allegedly confident that is not the case.

#1793. ‘This is what we dreamed of’ – Pochettino thrilled with USA farewell

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino reflected on a dream ending to his United States tenure as he prepares to take over at Manchester United.

Pochettino was appointed as Man Utd's new head coach last week, but he stayed on to oversee the USA's CONCACAF Nations League two-legged quarter-final tie with Haiti.

The USA romped to a 6-0 win on Saturday, and then followed it up with a routine 2-0 success in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

Pochettino, who took over in 2024, bows out having overseen a six-game unbeaten run since the end of the USA's World Cup campaign.

The USA had 14 shots worth a combined 1.43 expected goals, and enjoyed 74.2% possession. Christian Pulisic scored a stunning overhead kick, while Julian Hall netted his fifth goal in the space of six caps; at 18 years and 238 days old, he is the youngest player ever to net five goals for the USMNT.

"The way we played, that is what we dreamed of when we arrived," Pochettino told reporters.

"When you talk about these games, it looks like it was easy. But Haiti is a World Cup team. The players make the job easier.

"We knew that we have talented players, and in the last six games, being unbeaten and playing against a tough opponent, I see the team really enjoy playing football, playing soccer."

Electric atmosphere @TQLStadium tonight! https://t.co/1e4pIsZnJR

— U.S. Soccer Men's National Team (@USMNT) November 18, 2026

And Pochettino has no doubt that the future is bright for the USA, even if he will not be the coach at the helm.

"I am sure that this group of players, they will achieve big things in the future. I have no doubt," he said.

"[Experienced] players with a mix of younger, with the talent that is coming, I think it's a perfect combination.

"The way that they are leading all the things now, I think it's about being proud of the players, the whole squad, the whole pool of players.

"Of course, it's tough because it's emotional, because I really love these guys and I love the players, I love the staff, I love you, the fans and everything.

"And even if sometimes we have not agreed in our way to see things, that is life, to accept the critics, to accept that someone can disagree with you, with your ideas and see things in a different way. But that is life and you grow through there."

Steve Cherundolo will take charge of the USA's final game of 2026 in December, when they take on Jamaica in a friendly, with a new permanent coach expected to be in place for the CONCACAF Nations League semi-final against Mexico in March.

#1792. GdS: ‘Milan choose their next star’ – Cardinale prepares €70m for the January window

AC Milan proved that they are willing to spend money on talent in the summer and in January, it’ll seemingly be no different.

There was a shift in the works at Milan in the summer. No longer were the club going to focus solely on buying quantity over quality, hoping for a gem. Instead, they were going to buy quality and so far, it’s largely paying off.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, the roadmap is there to do the same again in a few months.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, as seen below, Cardinale is ready to invest around €70 million. After the €150m spent in the summer, it represents a substantial season of investment from the American and it seems this will be the trend moving forward.

There are currently decisions being made about who arrives, but it seems more likely that a new striker will be chosen and there are two standout names for the Rossoneri; both aren’t unfamiliar, too.

On one hand, you have Endrick and the other, you have Nicolo Tresoldi.

Starting with the former, the relationship between Roc Nation and Cardinale is strong, which could help negotiations. Of course, the American was also very keen to sign him in the summer mercato, so this interest stretches back.

They will have to compete with Roma, but to help give them the upper hand, they have involved Kaka in the process. The Brazilian – also an evangelical Christian – could do with Endrick ‘what Leonardo did with him’.

Cardinale plans to offer a loan with a buy clause to help sweeten the deal, and this could be worth €60m, plus bonuses. Importantly, he’d also be willing to offer Real Madrid a buy-back clause, similar to the Nico Paz situation.

With Tresoldi, things aren’t as simple. Their admiration is well known – as is the striker’s for the Diavolo – but they are not alone in their interest. His future lies away from Belgium, but the path is difficult to know.

Ideally, they wouldn’t sell him in January, but if a compelling offer arrives, he could well leave the club in the New Year. It may also be problematic if Premier League clubs become involved; they are desperate to avoid an auction.

#1791. Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Jurgen Klopp sends clear message that spells trouble for Nations League rivals

By Oliver Thomas | 17 Nov 2026 09:46

Jurgen Klopp is in dreamland after witnessing a “truly extraordinary” performance from his Germany side in a statement 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday.

The four-time world champions began the night sitting third in League A Group 2 and knew that they had to claim maximum points against the Oranje at the summit to secure top spot and qualify for the quarter-finals.

With so much at stake heading into the sixth and final matchday, Die Mannschaft rose to the occasion in prolific fashion, claiming their biggest win against their Dutch neighbours since 1959 when they won 7-0.

Derry Scherhant opened the scoring just before half time with a sensational maiden international goal, setting the tone for a dominant second-half display.

Overwhelmed by Germany’s relentless high press, the Netherlands had no answer as two goals from Florian Wirtz, and strikes from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda, sealed a statement triumph for Klopp’s side.

“What we’ve just witnessed was truly extraordinary,” the former Liverpool manager told reporters post-match. “The game was extraordinary, and incredibly difficult.”

“Against a really good opponent, you have to find a way to win. We had to adapt and make a few adjustments, some fairly significant ones, but we made them. We took away a lot of their strengths, and then we scored some incredible goals. That was unbelievable.

“It was a fantastic football match and a wonderful experience. I wouldn’t have ever dreamed of having the chance to do this in Berlin in front of a sold-out crowd. In the final international game of the year, it’s amazing.”

In addition to progressing to the quarter-finals, the result served as compelling evidence of Germany's renaissance and progress under Klopp, with his arrival fostering renewed optimism around his youthful squad.

Germany failed to win their opening two Nations League matches, but they ended their group campaign with 11 points (W3 D2 L1) and have conceded a competition-low three goals in six games.

"The moment I arrived here, I fell in love with this team at first sight,” said Klopp. “I'm at the beginning of this journey.

“I simply feel that we have a fantastic football team and a very good footballing idea that can work extremely well. If we can get these highly-talented players firing, then we're going to be a very difficult team to play against.

“We scored some incredible goals and, with increasing confidence, put in a great performance in front of a fantastic crowd. It’s been a lot of fun to work with this team, and we feel like we have a very special group of players here.

“But this is still only just the beginning – after six games, we can’t say that we’ve arrived where we want to be yet, as there are still lots of things we can improve on.”

"Everyone who was here today is going home with a smile, and won't be questioning the German national team for the next three or four months. That's a good thing," Klopp added when referring to the negativity that lingered previously around the national team.

Looking ahead to the quarter-final draw on Friday, Klopp added: "The lads can head home now with a smile on their faces as the group winners. We’ll watch the draw later this week and wait and see what sort of crunch match we’ll get, as there are only strong teams left.”

Germany, who have risen to 11th in the FIFA World Rankings, will play their two-legged quarter-final tie in March 2027, with a first-placed finish in League A rewarded with a second leg on home soil.

#1790. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

#1789. Watch: Pulisic shines as Pochettino news dominates headlines – Captain America bags a brace vs. Haiti

Last night, AC Milan will have been very happy to see Christian Pulisic extending his fine goalscoring form with a brace for America.

The United States national team have certainly faced a rocky few days. Thanks to Manchester United parting ways with Michael Carrick, Mauricio Pochettino will leave his role as the head coach of the project after the international break, leaving them in a strange position currently.

However, that was not a problem for The Stars and The Stripes, who put six past Haiti in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League. Of course, who else would be key but Pulisic himself?

Playing as a number 10 in a 4-2-3-1 system – which will have pleased Milan’s coach, Ruben Amorim – Pulisic was instrumental, scoring a brace in just two minutes. After 62 minutes, he stepped up from the spot after drawing the penalty himself.

Then, just a minute later, he added a second and recorded his 35th goal for the USMNT in 91 appearances.

For the attacker, it extends his fine run of form and the second half of 2026 is proving to be much more fruitful than the first. In Serie A, he’s scored four goals and provided an assist in eight games, and he’s now grabbed two more for the national team. After missing the last camp, it’s another reminder of his importance.

With Pochettino departing, it’s clear that they’ll still be in fine hands, with Pulisic remaining key!

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

A few notes: 1. This first match (of two for the Nations League) was played in Miami, Florida, and counted as a home match for Haiti, as the ongoing gang violence in Haiti made it too dangerous for an international match to be played there.

2. South Florida has a very large Haitian population, and as a result, the stadium looked like it was 90% filled with Haitians and fans of Haiti. So yeah, it was a home match for Haiti.

3. Haiti can be a very physical and challenging team to play against, but two things helped here – they were missing something like five of their starters from their World Cup team, and the ref was actually somewhat decent in calling fouls properly, instead of the usual CONCACAF ref who lets everything go and turns the match into a mixed martial arts no holds barred cage fight.

4. It was only 1-0 at halftime, Haiti was pressing very hard and were very physical. But then they just collapsed after the foul on Pulisic and the PK.

5. The USMNT has never looked this good – as a longtime follower of the USMNT, I can clearly see Pochettino’s influence and his selection of players and his tactics finally coming into fruition. Too bad he is leaving.

6. Poch’s coaching, tactics, and selection of younger players actually look a lot like what Amorim is doing at Milan. And yes, in his first year with the USMNT, Poch took some losses to teams that the USMNT had been able to beat previously. Which should mean that Amorim’s system should start looking great next year.

7. Unfortunately for Pochettino, ManUre are completely packed with players on high wages that are poorly suited for his tactics. As ManUre are in a relegation fight and Poch generally takes at least a year to rebuild a team and fully implement his ideas, I would not be at all be surprised to see ManUre get relegated. Poch is not a specialist in fighting relegation.

#1788. Pickford still England’s number one over Trafford, claims Young

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jordan Pickford should still get the nod as England's number one goalkeeper over James Trafford, so says Ashley Young.

Thomas Tuchel has used this Nations League campaign to split time evenly between Pickford and Trafford.

Pickford has been England's undisputed number one since 2017, with the 32-year-old making 94 appearances and keeping 49 clean sheets.

Peter Shilton (125) is the only goalkeeper to have won more caps for England than Pickford, though he now has fierce competition from Leeds United shot-stopper Trafford, who made a string of fine saves to help the Three Lions beat Spain on Sunday.

Pickford has now not started four of England's last seven competitive internationals, having only not been in the XI for two of their previous 41 beforehand.

However, in their last nine competitive matches without Jordan Pickford, England have only kept two clean sheets and conceded an average of two goals per game (18 in total).

And even though Trafford's performance saw plenty of calls for the 24-year-old to be installed as England's first-choice goalkeeper, Young has backed his former Everton club-mate Pickford.

"You've always got to give goalkeepers the chance to show what they're about," Young said on The Overlap Daily.

"Playing as a defender, you want to know who's behind you as a goalkeeper. Right, that's it, this is who's going to be our number one. That's who’s going to be in goal. And I think, rightly so, Jordan Pickford has earned 94 caps for a reason.

A POTM performance from James Trafford! https://t.co/LZY2ZZ7oSn

"He has been at three World Cups, two Euros; he’s got 49 clean sheets. It's understandable, but for me, Pickford is England's number one.

"Of course, Trafford has come in and done well, made some great saves at the end of the Spain game, but I think Pickford is a goalkeeper who shows himself more with his feet when playing for England, because Thomas Tuchel wants that, more passing out from the back and whatnot.

"I'm more confident in Pickford than Trafford with his feet. But when you've got different managers, it's different. At Everton, they play out from the back at times but not as much as England do. For me, Pickford's England's number one."

Trafford has impressed for Leeds this season, although he did make an error leading directly to a goal when his mistake was pounced on by Evanilson in Leeds' recent defeat to Bournemouth.

Nevertheless, Trafford has a goals prevented figure of 4.4, which is the joint-best in the Premier League, along with Brighton's Bart Verbruggen.

Trafford's 82.2% save ratio also tops the charts in the division.

Pickford, meanwhile, has registered a 73.7% save ratio, and 1.1 goals prevented.

#1787. Aston Villa transfer news: Newcastle United 'making strong moves' for Belgium international

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 09:54

Aston Villa and Newcastle United have reportedly identified Lille defender Nathan Ngoy as a potential transfer target.

Unai Emery's and Matthias Jaissle's sides went into the November international break sitting in 10th and 12th place respectively in the Premier League table.

Not only will both managers be disappointed with those positions, there will be concern that with their respective defensive records.

Villa have conceded 17 goals from their 10 top-flight fixtures in 2026-27, while the Magpies have shipped one goal fewer.

Therefore, strengthening in that area of the pitch has become a priority for the two managers ahead of 2027.

According to MilanNews24, Villa and Newcastle are 'making strong moves' to sign Belgium international Ngoy.

In sharp contrast to the two Premier League clubs, Lille have only conceded seven goals in 10 Ligue 1 fixtures, with Ngoy featuring in nine of those matches.

The 23-year-old has quickly become an established figure for his country, starting all six of their recent UEFA Nations League matches and scoring in the 4-1 win over Italy on Sunday.

While he possesses a contract at Lille until 2029, it remains to be seen whether Lille would be able to reject any substantial offers for his signature.

AC Milan have also been credited as admirers of the former Standard Liege player, who can deputise at right-back when required.

Although Villa signed Taylor Harwood-Bellis during the summer, he has not been viewed as a like-for-like replacement for Ezri Konsa.

Instead, Emery has been relying on three centre-backs in Victor Lindelof, Pau Torres and Tyrone Mings who are all aged between 29 and 33, essentially ensuring that alternatives will eventually need to be found.

Newcastle are in a similar position, with Fabian Schar and Dan Burn both aged 34 and right-back Tino Livramento having suffered regular injuries.

In both cases, Ngoy could become a first-team player should he move to Villa Park or St James' Park next year.

#1786. Maldini admits career could’ve been different without father and Liedholm: “Liked playing goalkeeper”

Things could’ve been much different for Paolo Maldini at AC Milan without two major figures in his life and career.

Maldini has two faces at Milan, but both remain adored by the fanbase. Firstly, you have the legendary defender, whose number was retired with him, a sign of respect and a chance to honour a career and legacy which surpasses many in the game.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, he returned as the sporting director, ending the Scudetto drought. Of course, that story didn’t have an ending as romantic as his playing career, but his legacy lives on. In fact, he may be voted into the Hall of Fame in the very near future.

Speaking to Tuttomercatoweb, via PianetaMilan, Maldini looked at the earliest stages of his career, as well as when he really took off for the Rossoneri.

“When my father took me to try out for AC Milan, I liked playing goalkeeper, but luckily I ended up choosing to be a defender. I played football with my friends in the park and at the youth club: I didn’t feel like I was destined for success at all, and until the day I made my debut, I never thought I could reach the highest levels.

“My dad always told me that the most important thing is to have fun, because if you treat it only as a job, it loses its magic.”

“There’s one person in particular who believed in me and wanted me to play when I was 15: Nils Liedholm, then AC Milan’s coach. He loved showing his faith in young players, and once, during a break, he asked me whether I preferred to play on the right or left. I replied that it was obviously his choice, but it was a gesture that helped me a lot.”

As they say, one change and the rest is history. With Maldini, that was certainly the case.

#1785. Record-breaking Harry Kane belongs in the company of greats that he keeps. There is only one gap in his record now and he remains as central to ending 60 years of hurt than he has ever been, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 16:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 20:17 EST, 12 November 2026

Only giants have trodden the path that Harry Kane walked at Wembley on Thursday when he strode out on to the pitch on a bitterly cold winter night, his four young children by his side, and beheld the array of trophies, honours, adulation and respect that awaited him.

It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and said 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.

Now, it sat before him on a plinth and Kane broke away from the England line-up and walked forward to hoist it aloft. He showed it to all the corners of the stadium and for a moment, it was framed against the giant tifo bearing his image and the words 'England's Finest' that towered over one end of the ground.

But the Ballon d’Or is old news in the flood of honours that is coming Kane’s way in this golden summer of a great career. Kane had become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or for a quarter of a century and on Thursday night he was to break the 37-year-old record held by Peter Shilton for the most England caps. He scored the winner, too. Of course, he did.

The occasion of England-Croatia in the Nations League was Kane's 126th appearance in an England shirt and Shilton stepped forward to hand him a small case containing a crest to mark the achievement. Finally, the Prince of Wales showed his appreciation to the England captain by presenting him with a commemorative shirt with 'Kane 126' emblazoned on it.

It was a night to feel the weight of football's history and the ghosts of greatness that people England's heritage. Kane belongs in the company he now keeps. He belongs in the pantheon of the game because he is one of the deadliest strikers in history. He belongs in the pantheon because of the humility he has shown and the dedication he devotes to improvement.

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking England appearance with a finely struck penalty

Before kick-off, Kane's history-making was celebrated with a commemorative shirt by the Prince of Wales

England (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; Alexander-Arnold 6 (White 78, 6), Quansah 4, Burn 6, Hall 7; Rice 5 (Garner 78, 5), Anderson 6; Rogers 8, Bellingham 6, Gordon 5 (Ngumoha 78, 5); Kane 7

Croatia (4-2-3-1): Livakovic 5; Smolcic 6 (Marco Pasalic 76 5), Stanisic 6, Vuskovic 6, Gvardiol 5; Misic 5 (Modric 76, 6), Kovacic 6; Sucic 7 (Mario Pasalic 70, 5), Baturina 6, Vlasic 5; Matanovic 5 (Budimir 70, 5)

He belongs with Billy Wright, the first England player to 100 caps, and the man who set the England appearance record at 105 when he played for his country for the last time in 1959. He belongs with Bobby Charlton, who made it to 106 before the heartbreak of the 1970 World Cup quarter-final defeat to West Germany brought his international career to an end.

Kane belongs with Bobby Moore, Charlton's rival as the greatest England player of all time, who reached the new mark of 108 caps in November 1973. That was one of the great numbers in English sport until Peter Shilton finally surpassed it. He reached 125 caps by the time he played his last game for England in the third-place play-off at the 1990 World Cup.

It is quite some lineage. And now it is Kane who holds the prize. And if this was hardly a momentous match, it was a momentous occasion. If you are tired of glorying in a player like Kane, a relentless striker, a wonderful passer, the sweetest striker of the ball you will ever see, a player of vision, a man who exudes the beauty of simplicity and the wonder of modesty, then you are tired of football.

The honours are rushing at him in a giddy, babbling flood. It may be that he reaches close to 200 caps before he retires and even if it already seems likely that that record will be broken by Jude Bellingham, who has 61 caps at the age of 23, Kane's England goals tally, which stands at 92 after another goal against Croatia, will not be under threat for a generation or longer.

The gap, of course, is a tournament victory. That is what still separates Moore and Charlton from him. Kane is a dream of a player but he has not won the World Cup or the European Championship. What remains is the hope that he will put that right in the years that he has left in the game.

Winning the Nations League would not be quite the same but it would be a start and this victory over Croatia took England a small step closer to that goal. A convincing win over Spain in Madrid on Sunday would take them closer to their aim of finishing top of this group and getting a favourable draw in the quarter-finals in the spring.

Kane made his England debut in March 2015 when he was 21 and England's future looks brighter now than it did when he broke through. More than an hour before the game, the men who will follow Kane and perhaps even chase his caps record, chatted animatedly on the pitch. Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Gibbs-White are the new breed.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour and celebrated with his trademark cold celebration

England had found themselves pegged back by Croatia after slopping defending drew the visitors level

Referee Morten Krogh was summoned to the monitor to review the penalty shout on Thursday

Kane returned to Wembley triumphant for the first time since his historic Ballon d'Or win

After the Kane festivities, the first half was an anti-climax. Twenty-four minutes of relative drudgery ensued before Kane exhibited the breadth of his talent once again to help put England ahead. He got the ball 30 yards out, looked up and drifted a beautiful diagonal pass out to the right and into the path of Bellingham. Bellingham volleyed it across goal and Rogers forced it over the line.

The second half began slowly, too, but 15 minutes into it, Croatia equalised. England failed to clear a corner, Jarell Quansah tried to head the ball back to Jordan Pickford and, as Kane watched on, Petar Sucic stole in and hooked the ball past the England goalkeeper into the roof of the net.

Quansah made some kind of amends three minutes later when he was dragged down in the box and Danish referee Morten Krogh awarded a penalty. It was Kane-time again. Kane took the kick and lifted it gently and with a touch of curl down the centre of the goal. Dominic Livakovic dived to his left and the ball sailed softly over his trailing leg and into the net.

Croatia had chances to draw level but could not take them. England made changes and young Rio Ngumoha, a winger of rare talent, another with a rich future ahead of him, another who will help to fill the void when the day comes for Kane to bid farewell to England, came on as a late substitute for Gordon.

And so Kane's night of history began to draw to a close. In a 2-1 victory, he had made one and scored one. He remains as central to England's hopes of ending more than 60 years without a trophy as he ever has been. In a career that has festooned him with garlands and left no one in doubt of his greatness, it is the only gap that remains.

Harry Kane has set his sights firmly on rapidly reaching a century of international goals after becoming England’s most-capped player of all time.

The England skipper marked his 126th appearance for the Three Lions with the winner against Croatia in the Nations League – his first goal since picking up the Ballon d’Or last month.

Kane was afforded an emotional presentation pre-match at Wembley to mark both achievements and is already thinking of creating more history after moving within eight goals of a ton.

‘It’s achievable,’ Kane said. ‘I’m getting closer. Breaking the appearance record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo at the stadium and having my kids with me was beyond dreams.

‘It’s important to recognise our great players. It’s maybe something we haven’t done so well over the years with some of our other greats.

‘It's been a crazy few weeks. I don’t know if I’ve fully taken it all in. The reception has been overwhelming.

‘Maybe during the winter break I’ll be on a beach reflecting on everything I’ve achieved, having a drink with my wife.’

Croatia legend Luka Modric, 41, was part of the presentations ahead of kick off and Kane did not rule out attempting to prolong his career in a similar vein to the AC Milan midfielder.

‘He’s an inspiration for a lot of us,’ Kane added. ‘An incredible player and a great person, he’s looked after himself and still to be playing at this level is inspiring for me to push the limits. To see where your body and mentality takes you.

‘As long as I feel I can help, I’ll be here for as long as I can. If that’s until I’m 40, we’ll wait and see.’

Now qualified for the quarter-finals, England need to beat Spain in Madrid on Sunday to top their group and Thomas Tuchel believes they can topple the world champions.

‘It’s a completely different scenario, completely different setup,’ Tuchel said. ‘But I'm very positive that we will get what we want.’

#1784. Why Arsenal are the ideal destination for Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 10:28

Arsenal have been interested in the profile of Eli Junior Kroupi for many months, and the forward should be one of the talking points of the next January transfer window. The London club have everything to be the ideal destination for the young France international.

Author of a very good 2025-26 season with Bournemouth in his first year in the Premier League, Kroupi scored 13 goals in 33 league matches. The 20-year-old striker was a revelation and quickly appeared on the radar of Europe’s biggest clubs.

‘Last summer, a fifth metatarsal injury compromised a possible departure, which the player was considering,’ - RMC Sport reported. The French outlet says the former Lorient player will be one of the attractions of the next summer transfer window, as he still interests heavyweights.

Kroupi has only just returned from his injury, however. He has played just four cameos with Bournemouth, but he reminded everyone of the extent of his talent with France. The 20-year-old won his first two caps and scored his first goal for France against Turkey (2-1).

During that international gathering, the forward made an impression and is considered one of the positives. He is highly rated by Zinedine Zidane’s staff, RMC Sport points out. His status is therefore potentially already changing, and that is before his expected transfer next summer.

For this important next step in his career, Arsenal have everything to be the ideal destination. While PSG, Barcelona and Bayern Munich are also interested in his profile, Arsenal have been trying to sign him for many months. Mikel Arteta is described as a fan of the new France international by TalkSport.

A move to the London club would allow Kroupi to stay in the Premier League. It is the biggest league in the world and he has already found his feet there with his 13 goals in his first season. Arsenal also appear to be still looking for a number nine, with Kroupi seen as their ‘ideal candidate’.

Viktor Gyokeres has failed to establish himself at the London club.

A departure is already being talked about for the next January transfer window. Kroupi’s profile is also compatible with Arteta’s style of play, as the Frenchman is a quick, technical striker with a great eye for goal.

Joining Arsenal would allow Kroupi to take an important step in his career by joining a top club. The English side are back among Europe’s best teams after their Premier League title win and Champions League final last year. It is one of the most attractive projects, along with that of PSG, at the moment.

However, in Paris, competition is strong at the tip of the attack with 2025 Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembele, who is set to extend his contract. The problem is the same at Bayern Munich with their 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who has also signed a new deal.

In London, Kai Havertz, who can notably be repositioned behind the centre-forward, represents less and more accessible competition for Kroupi.

#1783. Athletic: Fernandes still an option for Milan after second contract rejection – the situation

It seems Bruno Fernandes could still be an option for AC Milan, with the star rejecting two contract offers from Manchester United.

In the summer, Milan were rumoured to be interested in a move for Fernandes, who’d always seemed to be a fan of Ruben Amorim. So, with the continuous links to Portuguese players, the Manchester United captain being linked made even more sense.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, no move was made, with him not being seen as a priority, but that may change.

According to The Athletic, via MilanPosts on X, the Portuguese star could still be an option for the Rossoneri in the upcoming mercato(s). Earlier this week, it was reported – again by The Athletic – that he’d rejected a second offer from the Red Devils, so his future is more than up in the air.

The €65 million release clause will not be able to be used, as it expired in the summer. So, the Diavolo may have to be clever with how they negotiate for a player on the wrong side of 30. With his deal up in the summer, though, things get more interesting, even if Manchester United have the option of a year’s extension.

Mauricio Pochettino – who will arrive after the international break – could change his position, and Fernandes is believed to be waiting for an impact to be made with the new coach. If they don’t click, though, Milan could be waiting on the other side.
