#1704. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who said: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56

Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

Chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ

On the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink said on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh

Tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

Reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09

A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

"Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day

Asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”

Dan James passes a late fitness test to make Daniel Farke’s starting XI.

📋 Tonight's Starting XI pic.twitter.com/MQKQtGZm8c

Reggie Watson, 16, son of former Wigan midfielder Ben (of 2013 FA Cup final fame), makes his full Chelsea debut and becomes the club’s fourth youngest player. Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Danny Welbeck replace Alonso’s thrilling forward three, who are on the bench.

Chelsea XI Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck

Your Blues to face Leeds United in the #CarabaoCup! #CFC pic.twitter.com/636SOiUXVB

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1702. Rayan to Liverpool or Manchester United? How the Brazilian’s style suits both clubs

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:16

Rayan is living a fast-moving career in European football. Signed by Bournemouth in January 2026 after standing out at Vasco da Gama, the Brazilian forward quickly won a place in the Premier League and began attracting the attention of bigger clubs. Liverpool are already monitoring his progress, while a statement has put Manchester United in the conversation: the player revealed that he has always supported the Red Devils because of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Andoni Iraola, who worked with Rayan at Bournemouth, took charge of Liverpool at the start of 2026-27. Manchester United have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, a manager known for developing young attackers and for implementing a high-intensity style. But which of the two clubs would be the better destination for the Brazilian? The answer depends less on Rayan’s personal preference and more on the characteristics that have made him one of the most interesting prospects in Brazilian football.

Bournemouth paid Vasco €35m (about £30m) in January 2026, betting on a 19-year-old forward. Adaptation was quick: Rayan scored five goals and provided two assists in 15 games in the second half of last season.

His profile is different from a traditional winger who relies on short dribbles and quick changes of direction to beat a marker. Rayan is a player of strength and acceleration. When he receives with space, he can carry the ball at speed, protect possession with his body and attack the box with few touches.

In the 2025 Brazilian Serie A, Rayan was the player who finished the most carries with a shot, with 33 occasions. He also scored 14 goals in the league, a number that placed him among the competition’s top scorers. The forward is not just a winger who cuts inside, however. Under Fernando Diniz at Vasco, he was also used centrally, as a centre-forward, and showed an ability to win aerial balls and shield possession with his back to goal. His height and physical strength make it possible to imagine growth in that role, although he still has to improve his control and combination play under pressure.

It is also important to consider what is left to develop. Rayan can still improve the quality of his final pass, his choice of moments to shoot and his involvement in building play. Despite the volume of carries that ended in shots, his creative output was more limited. That helps explain why he still needs an environment that gives him freedom to attack without requiring him to be the main organiser of the attack.

This season, the Brazilian has played ten Premier League games, with one goal and no assists. The output does not match his arrival in England, but Rayan remains a frequent starter and is still adapting to a new manager and a model different from Iraola’s.

Liverpool’s interest strengthened after Iraola’s arrival. The Reds followed the Brazilian closely early in the season and could consider a move in 2027. Iraola knows Rayan’s virtues and limitations. It was under his management that the Brazilian began adapting to the intensity of the Premier League, playing mainly on the right and being given freedom to attack space.

The manager also played a part in the step up of other Bournemouth players, such as Antoine Semenyo, who stood out before moving to Manchester City. Tactically, the combination makes sense. Iraola’s teams usually press high, try to win the ball back in advanced areas and accelerate as soon as they find space. He does not demand that his wingers stay tied to the touchline: they can attack inside, combine with the full-backs and appear in different channels. Rayan could play on the right, cutting inside onto his left foot, but also attack depth and offer a physical threat in transitions.

At Liverpool, that characteristic could be useful. The team has changed in attack: Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha offer alternatives, but Rayan would add a different profile, a more powerful forward able to carry the ball at speed and attack the box.

There is one caveat. Liverpool already have quality attacking options. The manager also has to manage a more demanding calendar and a team with title ambitions. Rayan could find a way to play, but would hardly have the same freedom as a young player developing at Bournemouth.

Rayan’s link with Manchester United came to light in an interview with ESPN. The forward said he has always supported the club in England because of Cristiano Ronaldo, his great idol. He also recalled the emotion of playing at Old Trafford and beating the Red Devils 3-0 with Bournemouth in October.

The statement became relevant when United hired Pochettino to try to reorganise a team going through a difficult season. The Argentinian has a track record of developing young players and built his best work in England with intense teams, aggressive in the press and quick in transitions. His most usual model starts from a 4-2-3-1, with wingers who often attack inside spaces and full-backs who push on to give width.

That structure could favour Rayan. Starting from the right, the Brazilian would have freedom to carry towards the box, finish with his left foot and attack the spaces created by team-mates’ movement. High pressing also suits his physical ability, although defensive involvement is still an area he needs to improve.

The problem is competition. United already have Bryan Mbeumo, Amad Diallo and Matheus Cunha among their attacking options, plus Benjamin Sesko as a central reference. There is also a developmental question. Pochettino usually demands a lot from his players without the ball and works with coordinated attacking movements. For a forward who still needs to improve decision-making and creation, the environment can be positive but also brings high demands. The Brazilian would need to learn to alternate individual carrying with quick combination play and movement without the ball.

United, on the other hand, could offer room to grow if Pochettino sees Rayan as a medium-term project and not an immediate solution to attacking problems. The Argentinian’s ability to develop young forwards is a point in favour, but the squad already has players in similar roles.

Between the two scenarios, Liverpool appear to offer the clearer fit. Iraola already knows the Brazilian, knows how to use his strength in transitions and has a model that favours attackers able to carry the ball at speed. The departure of Mohamed Salah has also opened space for a reorganisation of the right side, making the position a concrete possibility for Rayan.

Manchester United have the emotional appeal and a manager whose philosophy could match the Brazilian’s characteristics. But the presence of Mbeumo, Amad and Cunha makes the battle for space more complex. To turn admiration for the club into a transfer, Rayan would need to see a clear sporting plan.

At any rate, the moment is still one of development. At 20, the forward does not need to choose immediately between two giants, especially as he has a contract with Bournemouth until 2031 and is still gaining experience in a demanding league. Rayan has the attributes to reach a top-level club, but his next step needs to be defined by the project that best uses his potential. Between his familiarity with Iraola and his identification with United, Liverpool appear to have a tactical advantage.

#1701. Report: Zlatan Ibrahimovic eager to sign Liverpool star, talks look certain

Zlatan Ibrahimovic is reportedly eager to sign a Liverpool star. Talks look absolutely certain at this point as AC Milan look to move.

AC Milan are looking to rebuild a bit after slumping post-title win in 2022. They've only won Serie A twice since 2004, in fact, and Zlatan Ibrahimovic played a role in both.

He was the star back in 2011. He'd signed there from Barcelona, getting out of the way of an emergent Lionel Messi and winning the Scudetto with a third Italian side. Ibrahimovic would then rejoin the club as the last stop in his career, scoring eight times as they won the title in 2022.

And now the Swede is involved again, though not as a player. He's helping to lead the club from a director's role, essentially as a proxy for the club's ownership.

The position has him lining up a bold move for one Liverpool star, too. Or maybe even more than that.

Gazzetta Dello Sport claim that Milan have Virgil van Dijk high on their shortlist. The Italian giants hope the Liverpool captain fancies a move there at the end of the season when his contract expires.

It’s an interesting one. Milan know they stand no chance of winning a financial race for Van Dijk. Clubs elsewhere can offer far more money but they feel the sentimental battle might be in their favour.

Van Dijk has made no secret about his admiration for Paolo Maldini and Alessandro Nesta in the past. The historic centre-backs of previous Milan sides might just appeal to him - certainly, that’s the hope.

The report mentions that Ibrahimovic himself is also pushing hard for the move. Talks look near-certain, too, given it’s only a month-and-a-half until Van Dijk is completely free to talk with non-English clubs.

So this is one to watch. It’ll all depend on what Van Dijk wants from what it almost certainly his final major contract in football and a final chance to lock down time chasing for elite honours.

No one seems to have a proper idea of what he’ll actually do. We’re still hoping that Liverpool persuade him to stay, of course.

#1700. Vitoria vs Bragantino - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 17 Nov 2026 18:17

Vitoria will be looking to end a five-match winless run when they welcome Bragantino to the Estadio Manoel Barradas on Thursday in a Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A encounter.

The hosts sit 15th in the table with 38 points from 34 matches, just one point above the relegation zone, while Braga occupy eighth place with 47 points and are hoping to keep their hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Copa Libertadores alive.

Vitoria head into Thursday's encounter under pressure after losing 3-0 at home to Fluminense in their most recent league outing, a result that extended their winless run to five matches.

The Rubro-Negro had previously suffered a 2-0 defeat away to Coritiba, following consecutive 1-1 draws against Athletico Paranaense and Corinthians, while their earlier meeting with Sao Paulo ended in a 2-1 loss.

Their last league victory came on October 8, when they thrashed Chapecoense 4-0 at home, leaving them with only two points from the last five matches, the fewest points by any team in the league in that period.

The defeat to Fluminense also marked a difficult end to Jair Ventura's time in charge, with the coach dismissed after Vitoria slipped to within one point of the relegation zone.

Rafael Lacerda has been appointed and will take charge of his first match on Thursday, having had the international break to work with the squad and prepare for the challenge ahead.

Vitoria's home record offers some encouragement, however, as they have won 10 of their 17 league matches at the Barradao, drawing twice and losing five times, though they are without a win in their last two games as hosts.

Bragantino, meanwhile, arrive in Salvador after recording consecutive victories, having beaten Chapecoense 3-0 before securing a 2-1 home win over Santos in their most recent match.

Massa Bruta took the lead against Santos via an own goal from Rodinei, before conceding an equaliser in the 37th minute, but Wallace Yan scored his third goal in two games to claim all three points.

Vagner Mancini's side have now won three of their last five league matches, drawing once and losing once, with their other victory coming in a 4-2 home success over Cruzeiro, while they recorded a 1-1 draw away to Remo during that period, with their only defeat coming against Palmeiras, who beat them 2-0 in Sao Paulo.

Braga’s away form has been less convincing than their home performances, having won only four of their 17 matches on the road, drawing five and losing eight, while they are without a win in their last eight league games and last 10 across all competitions.

However, the head-to-head record also gives the visitors reason for optimism, having won the last two meetings between the clubs, though the Massa Bruta have lost the last two on the road.

Vitoria will be without several players through injury, including Nathan Mendes, Fabiano Souza, Edu, Camutanga, Ramon and Riccieli, while Dudu is also listed as unavailable.

Luan Candido and Nacho Laquintana are expected to miss out because they are on loan from Bragantino and their agreements reportedly include clauses requiring Vitoria to pay a fee for each player to feature against their parent club.

Emmanuel Britez is available again after serving a suspension, and the defender is expected to partner Caca in central defence.

Lacerda is also likely to retain Lucas Arcanjo in goal, with Rene, Erick and Matheuzinho among the attacking options as he prepares for his first match in charge.

Bragantino will be without Lucas Barbosa, who is suspended, while Rodriguinho and Davi Gomes are sidelined through injury.

Jose Hurtado is also a doubt after picking up a thigh injury, leaving Mancini with some decisions to make in defence as he attempts to maintain his team's recent momentum.

Yan is expected to retain his place in the attacking midfield, while Eduardo Sasha should lead the line.

Arcanjo; Mateusinho, Caca, Brítez, Jamerson; Goncalves, Martinez, Baralhas; Erick, Matheuzinho; Rene

Volpi; Augusto, Marques, Rodríguez, Capixaba; Fabinho, Ramires; Mosquera, Yan, Herrera; Sasha

Lacerda's appointment could provide Vitoria with a lift, especially with the match taking place at the Barradao, where they have won 10 times this season.

However, Bragantino's recent improvement should allow them to compete, and we expect both sides to find the net before sharing the points.

#1697. Fighter who ambushed UFC star in bloody hotel brawl is punished: Abu Dhabi court dishes out six-month prison sentences and fines - including £61k for filming shocking attack

Published: 09:58 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:57 EST, 13 November 2026

Usman Nurmagomedov and his entourage have been swiftly punished with prison sentences and fines in Abu Dhabi after their shocking hotel attack.

Nurmagomedov set upon UFC star Merab Dvalishvili on Wednesday, slapping him in the lobby of Yas Hilton hotel in a revenge mission filmed by his friends.

The Georgian-American Dvalishvili then retaliated and fought back with his cameraman as the melee rapidly descended into complete mayhem. Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised and the attackers were quickly detained by the authorities.

In just two days, their punishments have been decided by the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, who published the findings on social media.

Six of the attackers were given six-month prison sentences and ordered to pay £61,000 each in fines. They will also be immediately deported  when their sentences end.

They were described as having 'caused panic, disturbed public security and  endangered lives'.

Two of Nurmagomedov's associates were fined £10,000 each for 'disturbing public security and assaulting others'.

Usman Nurmagomedov (left) was the one who initiated the brawl by slapping Merab Dvalishvili - his brother Umar (right) lost a title shot against the Georgian last year

The Abu Dhabi court shared this post online confirming the punishments for the attackers

And the other two members of the group who recorded the assault were given six-month sentences, £61,000 fines and confiscation of the devices used.

Dvalishvili had been due to fight in a RAF wrestling event on Saturday. CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein released a statement confirming the fighter is back.

He said: 'I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.

'We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us.'

Nurmagomedov and his team's violent ambush was four months in the making.

Back in July, Dvalishvili was competing in a RAF event in Georgia, which is a freestyle wrestling show the UFC allow their fighters to compete in outside of the day job.

While milling around at the event, a Dagestani wrestler and friend of Umar, Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, confronted Dvalishvili about refusing to entertain a rematch of any kind with Umar.

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday

'I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody (Gadzhimagomedov) came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand,' Dvalishvili told Ariel Helwani.

'And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realize, "Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him?"

'It’s between me and Umar… I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads.'

After Gadzhimagomedov squared up to him, Dvalishvili shoved him in the neck, shouting: 'What's your problem, b***h!'

The situation, unlike the hotel brawl that escalated into a complete bloodbath, was quickly defused and there was a child in close proximity.

Usman wanted to take revenge on behalf of fellow Dagestani Gadzhimagomedov and also his brother Umar, who lost against Dvalishvili in a title shot last year.

In the footage of the hotel attack, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man said a couple of words to him and slapped him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

He tried to fight back but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too. Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview

He said in a video, bloody and bruised as he received treatment: 'What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

'You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.'

His companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'

Dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It shows your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. This is nothing for me, but it shows what kind of people you guys are. P***ys do this bro. We are warriors.'

#1696. Declan Rice’s new five-year deal to 2031 marks his rise from £105m signing to Arsenal leader

By Alexis Pereira | 17 Nov 2026 18:28

Declan Rice’s new contract with Arsenal recognises a transformation built over three seasons. When he arrived at the Emirates Stadium in July 2023, the midfielder was a high-impact signing: he cost £105m, a record for a British player at the time, and carried the expectation of lifting a team that had just lost the Premier League title to Manchester City.

Today, at 27, Rice is an English champion, one of the leaders of the dressing room and one of the team’s technical reference points. The new five-year deal shows Arsenal’s intention to keep him at the centre of the project through his physical and technical peak. It also reflects his changing status within the club, as Rice is expected to earn a salary close to that of Bukayo Saka, until now the squad’s top earner.

Rice was not just an expensive signing who lived up to expectations. He became a more complete player, widened his influence across different phases of play and took on responsibilities beyond his role in midfield. The promise of 2023 has become one of the faces of a championship team and a leader for the cycle that starts now.

Rice’s arrival came at a decisive moment for Mikel Arteta’s project. In 2022-23, Arsenal spent much of the season at the top but lost steam in the closing stretch and finished five points behind Manchester City. The team had shown that they could compete for the title, but they needed more quality, depth and experience to sustain a challenge to the end.

Rice had characteristics that answered several of those needs. At 24, he was already West Ham United’s captain, had experience with England and had just won the Conference League. Arsenal beat the competition and completed the signing for £100m fixed plus £5m in bonuses.

The fee raised expectations. It was not enough for Rice to be a good holding midfielder: he had to justify a historic investment and help Arsenal take the step needed to compete with City. His first season showed the scale of the signing quickly.

Rice played 38 Premier League games, scoring seven goals and providing eight assists. The number of goal contributions was a considerable improvement on his West Ham record, but his impact was not limited to attacking output. Arsenal again finished as runners-up, but Rice had already become one of the team’s most important players. The signing did not deliver an immediate title, but it helped turn expectation into a conviction that the club had found a midfielder able to carry their project for many years.

Rice’s development also reflects the way Arteta changed his use. Early in his time at Arsenal, the Englishman often played as the deepest midfielder, responsible for protecting the defence and offering a reference point for build-up. It was a familiar role, close to the one he had at West Ham, but it did not use his full repertoire.

After an adaptation period, especially from the start of 2024, Arteta began using him more often as a box-to-box midfielder on the left. The change let Rice use one of his main qualities: carrying the ball at speed, breaking lines and arriving in the opposition area while still contributing to defensive recovery.

The Englishman gained more freedom to attack space, appear at the edge of the box and join attacking combinations. His physical power became a weapon for taking Arsenal into the opposition half, while his ability to get back helped keep balance when the team lost the ball. Instead of just protecting team-mates, Rice also began to drive the team.

Set pieces were another important tool. Rice began taking corners and free-kicks, using the accuracy of his delivery and his ability to put the ball in dangerous areas. Since his arrival, he has provided ten assists from set pieces in the Premier League. His two free-kick goals against Real Madrid in the 2024-25 Champions League quarter-finals were the most emblematic moment of that evolution.

Versatility does not mean Rice has no fixed position or needs to take part in every attacking action. The most recent development lies in choosing moments. With Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard offering different partnership options, Arteta has alternated the height at which the Englishman receives the ball and the freedom he has to advance.

The ability to perform different roles is one of the reasons Rice has become so important to Arteta. In the title-winning season, he was used both as the most advanced midfielder and in a midfield pair alongside Zubimendi. He is not just a player who adapts to different positions: he lets the manager change the structure of the team without necessarily changing personnel.

Rice’s growth was not only tactical. Over the seasons, he also became one of the squad’s main voices. His direct personality, willingness to demand more from team-mates and ability to take responsibility in difficult moments made him a reference point for the group.

One example came in April, when Odegaard was out injured and Rice was given the captain’s armband. He had worn it on other occasions, but the choice reinforced a perception that had been building: his influence does not depend on being the official captain.

In Arsenal’s 2025-26 Premier League title, which ended a 22-year wait for the competition, Rice was one of the protagonists of the campaign, with 36 appearances, four goals and five assists in the league. More than his statistical contribution, his ability to maintain intensity in different roles was fundamental.

Declan Rice at Arsenal - all competitions since joining in July 2023 2023-24: 51 games, 48 starts, 33 wins, 8 draws, 10 defeats, 7 goals, 9 assists (64.7% wins) 2024-25: 52 games, 48 starts, 28 wins, 16 draws, 8 defeats, 9 goals, 10 assists (53.8% wins) 2025-26: 55 games, 49 starts, 37 wins, 12 draws, 6 defeats, 5 goals, 9 assists (67.3% wins) 2026-27 (in progress): 15 games, 14 starts, 13 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat, 1 goal, 5 assists (86.7% wins) Total: 173 games, 159 starts, 111 wins, 37 draws, 25 defeats, 22 goals, 33 assists (64.2% wins)

Trophies for Arsenal (3): Premier League 2025-26, Community Shield 2023, Community Shield 2026

Official matches only (Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, EFL Cup and Community Shield). Matches decided on penalties count as draws. Data up to 16 November 2026. Sources: FBref (Opta data), BeSoccer and Opta Analyst.

The challenge now is to sustain this level without ignoring fatigue. Rice has come from seasons with a high volume of games, often exceeding 50 matches for club and country. Last season, he played 54 games for Arsenal in all competitions, in addition to England commitments. Managing his workload will be important for him to keep his influence over a demanding calendar.

By extending his contract to 2031, Arsenal secure a player who still has years at his peak ahead and who already knows Arteta’s demands in depth. The club no longer need to wait for Rice to become a leader: that stage has already happened. Now the expectation is that he helps lead the next chapters of a project that intends to keep competing for the main trophies.

#1695. Moreira discusses first Belgium goal, ‘special’ Milan group and learning in Italy: “I’ll always remember”

Last night, Diego Moreira scored his first goal for Belgium and AC Milan will be very happy to see their investment continuing to shine.

It’s fair to say that Moreira has been a revelation for Milan. His arrival came out of nowhere, with a deal first reported by FootballKush and then it was picked up by the biggest sources in football. His first appearance was a struggle against Juventus, but the rest, as they say, is history.

Goals have come regularly, with huge appearances that have defined the Rossoneri’s season already. For example, the goal against Inter, with two assists to accompany it. He’s perhaps been the signing of the season in Italy and there’d maybe be a conversation about Europe, too.

After scoring against Italy, Moreira spoke to Sky, looking at the team’s performance, playing with Kevin De Bruyne and the feeling of grabbing his first goal for his country, as MilanNews relays.

“I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”

Mancini said that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team…

“We have some very strong players up front, like Doku, De Bruyne, but I think that in the end it’s a sport where everyone is needed and we all played a great game.”

What does it mean to play with a player like De Bruyne?

“De Bruyne is special; it’s a pleasure to have him with us because he sees things that others don’t see, he has a lot of experience and we’re happy to have him in our team.”

What do you take from this experience with the national team at AC Milan?

“I learned a lot in Italy because it’s a league with a lot of experienced players. Playing for the national team and for AC Milan are two very positive things, and I’m very happy.”

How do you recover in Europe after a difficult start?

“It’s difficult but we’re working towards this. We have to be prepared and we have players who will help us with this.”

Then, in the mixed zone, he was also intercepted by MilanNews, where he also answered a few questions about the Rossoneri.

Diego, you scored in your first Milan derby, just like Kaká, Shevchenko, and Ronaldinho before you. How have you settled in at AC Milan?

“I’m very happy. At AC Milan, I’m surrounded by a special group, with many great players. Having them around me helps me a lot, especially in terms of experience. It’s true, the match against Inter was special. I’ll continue to work hard and give my best.”

Good in Serie A, bad in the Europa League: why this two-faced Milan?

“I’m on the national team right now, and you’re asking me about Milan?”

Belgium practically overwhelmed Italy, your current footballing nation. It ended 4-1, but the scoreline could have been eight or nine goals…

“It’s something special, and we’re very happy. It was an important match, so winning and scoring was really nice.”

#1694. Opinion: Massive Real Madrid to Liverpool deal looks increasingly possible

Real Madrid appear ready to open the door to a massive sale. Liverpool can swoop in here and get themselves a proper star.

Liverpool need to invest in their midfield. That should be obvious to everyone now after a start to the season that demonstrated an incredible weakness there.

That's the result of building a midfield group entirely out of attacking players. All of Liverpool's options want to get further forward, leaving no one to really cover gaps or stop counter-attacks.

It's led to Andoni Iraola calling on Trey Nyoni to learn the holding role but even he is better known as a more advanced midfielder. It also just means that Liverpool are essentially relying on a teenager to keep their side secure - hardly ideal.

We fully expect Liverpool to move for a defensive, controlling midfielder in 2027. Maybe that's in January or maybe it's in the summer but either way, some sort of move simply must be on the way.

Real Madrid look ready to do businessThere's a midfielder we have our eyes on at Real Madrid: Eduardo Camavinga. He's been heavily linked to Liverpool in the past and his situation in Madrid is becoming less and less clear. Or rather, it's becoming more clear that he's not viewed as a long-term piece. That looked the case recently with Real Madrid reportedly eyeing a move for Martin Zubimendi - someone who would replace Camavinga in midfield.

There's a midfielder we have our eyes on at Real Madrid: Eduardo Camavinga. He's been heavily linked to Liverpool in the past and his situation in Madrid is becoming less and less clear.

Or rather, it's becoming more clear that he's not viewed as a long-term piece. That looked the case recently with Real Madrid reportedly eyeing a move for Martin Zubimendi - someone who would replace Camavinga in midfield.

That's how Liverpool can swoop in, offering the Frenchman the key role he deserves. We're massive fans of his, believing he's woefully underrated because of Aurelien Tchouameni's efforts in midfield for Real Madrid. The Reds simply won't find a better defensive midfielder.

So if Camavinga is available, and it increasingly looks like he will be after almost moving in the summer, then Liverpool have got to act. This is the one, to put it bluntly.

#1693. Flamengo vs Athletico Paranaense - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 17 Nov 2026 19:11

With four rounds remaining in the Brasileirao, Flamengo host Athletico Paranaense on Wednesday night, November 18, as their title defence enters its decisive stage.

Having collected 92% of the available points in the second half of the season, Flamengo can take a significant step towards back-to-back titles and put themselves in a stronger position ahead of their huge clash against Palmeiras in the following round. Athletico Paranaense, meanwhile, face an uphill task to break back into the top four, having gone four matches without a win and with the tournament's leading scorer unavailable.

In the fight for back-to-back titles and a ninth Brasileirao crown, Flamengo return from this FIFA international break with good news: their key players delivered excellent performances and, more importantly, came back from international duty without any injuries.

Giorgian de Arrascaeta once again took centre stage for the Rubro-Negro with the Uruguay national team. Having had a direct hand in both of Uruguay’s goals against Argentina at the Bombonera, Flamengo’s number 10 also became the first foreigner to have a bust unveiled at the club’s headquarters, in a ceremony on Sunday, November 15.

Bruno Henrique also received the honour and looked ahead to the business end of the season: “We know there is not much left before the year ends, there are four games, so we will give everything in these games to win the title. God willing, we can celebrate in December as well,” he said at the event.

Right-back Guillermo Varela, meanwhile, produced a solid display, playing the full 95 minutes of the match in Buenos Aires. Although Argentina’s goal came down his side, he was not at fault.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Ecuadorians Gonzalo Plata and Anthony Valencia did not leave the bench, but the latter two still have a friendly against Bolivia on Tuesday night, November 17.

Athletico Paranaense, for their part, are enjoying a notable campaign for a newly promoted side. However, in the fight for a direct spot in next season’s Libertadores, the Furacao suffered a heavy blow at Brazil’s sports court (STJD).

In a hearing on Monday, November 16, Kevin Viveros had his ban extended to three matches. The Brasileirão’s top scorer with 21 goals was sent off in the 3-1 defeat to Vasco on November 4, for a stamp on full-back Cuiabano.

As a result, he will not return until the final round, against Sao Paulo at the Arena da Baixada. Jorge Rivaldo and Renan Peixoto are the natural options given their profile, but manager Odair Hellmann could also opt to use forward Kerwin Vargas in an adapted role.

In the same hearing, the Parana side were also punished. The fine for racist gestures attributed to a fan during the match against Vasco was increased to R$30,000 (approximately £4,200). The decision was taken by a majority of votes.

Currently fifth with 54 points, Athletico could close the gap on Fluminense, who occupy the final Libertadores spot. Bahia and Atletico Mineiro, however, are also in the same points range.

In a late development, Gonzalo Plata was released from the Ecuador squad for “personal reasons” and could become an unexpected boost. Having played just 13 minutes against Costa Rica, he should not, in theory, show any physical wear.

Nicolas de la Cruz and Anthony Valencia remain with their national teams and are not expected to return in time.

On the medical front, experienced left-back Alex Sandro has recovered from muscular oedema in his left thigh and has returned to training with the group, although Ayrton Lucas is expected to be the first choice for Portuguese manager Leonardo Jardim.

Midfielder Lucas Paqueta has not yet fully recovered from a knee problem sustained during the thrashing of Vasco, so he is unlikely to be included without a reasonable amount of training, according to Jardim himself. Danilo, meanwhile, continues his recovery schedule following a jaw fracture and also remains sidelined.

The point of concern is the number of players one booking away from suspension: Leo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Erick Pulgar, Arrascaeta, Pedro, Bruno Henrique, Luiz Araujo and Vitao. Should any of them be booked by referee Rafael Klein, they would miss the clash against Palmeiras in the following round.

Besides Viveros, Dantas is also serving a suspension due to the automatic one-match ban for a third yellow card. Young centre-back Arthur Dias, who is attracting interest from several European clubs, is another absentee. He is set to play for the Brazil national team against Singapore and is not expected to return to Brazil in time.

Defender Lucas Esquivel is still recovering from a hip injury and will be assessed on matchday, but he is expected to complete the back line alongside Gaston Benavidez and Juan Aguirre. Goalkeeper Santos and Bruno Zapelli could be given a chance in the starting eleven.

Agustin Rossi; Varela, Leo Pereira, Leo Ortiz, Ayrton Lucas; Pulgar, Jorginho, Arrascaeta; Carrascal, Pedro, Samuel Lino. Manager: Leonardo Jardim.

Athletico Paranaense possible starting lineup:

Santos; Benavidez, Aguirre, Esquivel; Gilberto, Luiz Gustavo, Jadson, Mendoza; Bruno Zapelli, Joao Cruz, Kerwin Vargas. Manager: Odair Hellmann.

Athletico's task would have been difficult enough as it is, but with their top scorer and best defender both unavailable, it is hard to see the visitors taking anything from this encounter.

For Flamengo, the priority will be to maintain their formidable home record and head into the most eagerly anticipated game of the year in a favourable position. A convincing victory at the Maracana would be the ideal way to achieve that.

#1691. Mazzara: ‘A core of 16-18 high level players’ – Cardinale hopes to take Milan to new levels

Gerry Cardinale has invested heavily in AC Milan recently and there are no plans to slow down anytime soon.

Since the restructuring of the vendor loan, Cardinale has completely changed his ownership style. More actively involved, the American has seemingly fallen in love with the club and has become desperate to see it succeed.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Glimpses were seen before the mercato, with him regularly visiting the training ground. However, his work since then – spending €150 million on transfers and attending every Serie A game so far – shows the level of dedication he has to the cause.

In January, the American is expected to spend heavily, too. A €70 million bid for Endrick is being prepared, whilst he is also determined to sign Goncalo Inacio. It’s clear that he wants to raise the level of the starters and those who will contribute from the bench.

In an editorial for MilanNews today, Pietro Mazzara looked at the current squad and what Cardinale plans to do.

“AC Milan’s transfer market is poised for significant events because Gerry Cardinale has no intention of stopping. His comments in recent days, both public and private, are a clear statement of what the AC Milan owner intends to do to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“Whether he succeeds or not will only be determined by time and the type of decisions he makes, but he certainly has the desire, vision, and financial resources. One can expect anything from someone who beat out Netflix for the Warner Bros. acquisition.

“Among the many things he has learned is that the climate of mediocrity surrounding results has undermined the mentality of a club and an environment that, instead, must strive to always be at the top.

“But returning to those levels requires several factors: a clear decision-making structure (which will be finalised by Markus Krösche, who will always report to Cardinale, who will always have the final say and be involved in negotiations), strong players in the squad, a political presence in the halls of power, a connection with the fans, and credibility.

“What may seem like slogans in themselves are actually manifestos that one can legitimately believe or not. The only way to evaluate Cardinale’s work is to observe how he operates and then draw conclusions.

“He’s fired up, and between January and next summer there will be some serious transfer campaigns. The reason is simple: there’s a need to significantly raise the squad’s level, creating a core of 16-18 players of a certain caliber who can be joined by young players to develop and develop.

“This is why Milan will be looking for not only technically strong players, but also leaders who can complement those already in the Milan core group.

“It’s crucial to raise the team’s personality, including strong personalities who can provide a different kind of motivation during the day-to-day at Milanello. These players, inevitably, cost money, but Cardinale doesn’t want to set limits.

“This doesn’t mean Milan will sign a player worth one hundred million euros, but it does mean they can continue along the operational path laid out by Diego Moreira. All of this is in concert and in line with Ruben Amorim, who is fiercely defended by the AC Milan owner and with whom he intends to begin a long-term relationship.

“And the vision is to acquire the Van Dijks in the pre-prime phase rather than signing them at 35 (assuming, for the sake of argument, that I’d sign someone like that now).

“In my opinion, a Sandro Tonali- style signing is needed. And it’s not out of the question that Milan could try to bring him back in the coming years, even though he currently plays for a club as complex to negotiate with as Tottenham.

“Meanwhile, discussions are ongoing to finalise the renewal of Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse.”

#1690. Chelsea news: Estevao Willian provides fresh comments on playing time frustration after latest Brazil appearance

By Darren Plant | 17 Nov 2026 20:14

Chelsea winger Estevao Willian has thanked Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti for his "trust" during the international break.

The 19-year-old's lack of starts for Chelsea since the arrival of Xabi Alonso has been a regular topic of conversation.

Although the Spaniard placed more faith in the playmaker prior to the November international break, Estevao was still dropped after an encouraging performance versus Manchester United on October 31.

However, Ancelotti has recently insisted that Estevao's game time for Chelsea will not negatively impact on his role for the national team.

That stance has since been proven through the former Palmeiras starlet featuring for 128 minutes across friendlies versus Japan and Singapore.

During Tuesday's 7-0 win over Singapore, Estevao contributed one goal and two assists before his 70th-minute withdrawal.

Speaking to ESPN after the game, Estevao admitted that he was grateful for the support that he had received from Ancelotti.

He said: "I'm very happy to have gotten minutes in the friendlies.

"I thank Ancelotti for his confidence, because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I've had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation."

With Kallang - the venue for Tuesday's friendly - eight hours in front of England, Estevao is essentially getting extra rest ahead of Saturday's Premier League game versus Leeds United.

Nevertheless, not only will it take his body clock time to reset, the likes of Cole Palmer, Danny Welbeck and Emanuel Emegha - players competing for roles in the final third - have not represented their countries during the international break.

Meanwhile, Morgan Rogers was back in the country on Monday after representing England, so Estevao is essentially at a disadvantage when it comes to trying to dislodge teammates from the starting lineup.

All things considered, it is highly likely that he will take a place on the substitutes' bench.

#1688. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

81 - Kobbie Mainoo completed the most passes in Manchester United's 4-0 win over Sabah (81).It was the most by an Englishman for the Red Devils in a UEFA Champions League match since Michael Carrick in February 2014 vs Olympiakos (89).Mentor. pic.twitter.com/59wSvQydOG

Benjamin Šeško and Patrick Dorgu share their thoughts after Manchester United's successful return to Champions League football ✅🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/iKC58Po2Vx
